records.procedure:
NEW acquisition: with actual Animal Handling proficiency, select one already real willing/tamed Beast, noncorrupted, INT<7, that fits one of the three finite body templates below. Finding, buying or taming it requires actual campaign access/consent; the feat creates no animal, stocked shop or universal charm. Spend one uninterrupted hour together at touch range; one bond attempt per completedLR, noRP. One feat bond at a time. Use the template corresponding to the real animal's body/native movement; do not turn a dog into a bird or grant a new breathing mode. AC12+floor(ownerPB/2), maximumHP5+total owner level; template attack/ability/movement values are explicit NEW. At initial bond convert existing HP proportionally max(1,floor(newMax×oldHP/oldMax)); preserve actual conditions/injuries. Later maximum growth never heals, decreases clamp without damage. Ordinary legal healing works, but no Hit Dice/rest-refill is invented. Use one shared BA command within60ft while the animal can perceive you: in its attached phase after your regular turn, move and make its one attack or Dash/Disengage/Help/Dodge. No independent turn/Reaction; uncommanded move defensively and Dodge. The animal's HP-only chassis dies at0, producing its one actual corpse and ending the bond, with no Wound/death-save sequence; this is a feat-specific NEW rule, not generic animal law. Death/release never creates replacement: after a new completedLR, a new real animal and full hour are required. Voluntary release takes one uninterrupted hour and ends the bond without healing; preserve the same physical animal and restore its prior ordinary profile with the same current-HP fraction, not a fresh full animal. A creature cannot have this and a Ranger bond simultaneously; transferring requires actual release and new paid acquisition, not additive statistics. Owner death ends the bond and, if the animal remains alive, restores its saved ordinary profile using the same positive-HP ratio conversion as release; a dead animal remains its actual corpse. Temporary owner incapacity prevents new commands but does not cancel a previously committed legal command; after that command, uncommanded phases remain defensive. This never supplies autonomous attacks.
NEW explicit EX58 interface: retain one real creature identity and one current control/phase record. Riding, bonding or transferring custody does not clone a turn, movement budget, Reaction, attack allowance, body or resource pool. An attached companion acts in its source-defined phase after the owner’s regular turn; a controlled mount uses EX58’s actual mounted-phase procedure. A body fitting both roles elects one compatible route before that round’s work, preserves all already-spent allowances and cannot switch routes to gain a second phase. Its actual load, tack, rider geometry, mounting/dismounting cost and ordinary independent temperament remain. One shared Bonus Action command and one offensive companion action per owner per numbered round apply where those source engines impose them. This feat supplies no blanket override of a specific engine’s attack or no-resource restrictions.
The three supplied body templates are NEW complete feat chassis, not evidence that such a Beast is available. Use only the corresponding real body/native mode. Saved ordinary maximum/currentHP and original constituent identity are required before bonding; no missing oldHP record is replaced by invented full health. The feat’s0HP-death rule applies only to this feat chassis; an independently governed mount/Ranger chassis retains its own rules rather than taking both.
records.newChoices: Complete real-animal bond, three body templates, finite statistics, proportional conversion, command/HP-only death and no-free-replacement procedure.
workedCases: A ground companion bonded by level5 has max10HP. A real animal at half of its oldHP converts to5HP, not full10.
At0HP it dies and leaves its actual body. Taking a rest alone neither revives it nor creates another beast.

completeOriginalCatalogObject.name: False Comfort

operational.targets: One creature you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect.
operational.duration: Instantaneous sensation; pending distraction until consumed or its one-round endpoint. Ends at the end of the target's first future regular turn, excluding the entire current target turn if one is already in progress. Outside initiative, expires 6 elapsed seconds after application. Preserve the selected virtual marker or absolute deadline through initiative changes and absence; end-phase effects resolve before end-marker cleanup.
operational.resolution: The target makes a Wisdom save against your spell DC. Success: no new sensation or rider. Failure: it experiences a convincing subjective surge of relief or apparent recovery and receives disadvantage on its next actual Perception check before the endpoint. Consume the rider when that check begins, even if another source already imposes disadvantage or advantage cancels it.
operational.effect: The sensation can feel like warmth, easing pain or the beginning of healing. It restores no HP or temporary HP, stabilizes nothing, removes no Wound or condition and generates no healing/recovery event or trigger. Apparent comfort does not alter actual injury, damage, HP-dependent rules or knowledge made apparent by physical evidence. The target is never required to behave as though mechanically healed. One pending False Comfort distraction per target across all casters; a later failed save replaces it, while a later successful save leaves an existing rider intact.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, duration, targets, uses or information.
operational.limitations: The one-use rider names an actual Perception check; it does not independently lower passive Perception or require a new check. No Action/turn loss, forced movement, belief about a specific medical fact, magical diagnosis, cure, enduring pain suppression or permanent memory change is granted. If no qualifying check occurs before expiry, the rider ends unused. A successful replacement owns its new endpoint; stale cleanup cannot erase it. A failed or countered new cast creates no replacement, though independently required concentration/contact endings still occur. Actual class access, repertoire, components, costs, Dissonance/Refrain, beginning hooks, concentration transitions and counter windows follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base 0 RP does not waive Action/components or Refrain. A failed, blocked or countered cast refunds no committed cost and restores no old concentration. V is audible and S needs its normal usable hand; subtle names do not hide casting. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC, with ordinary binary save rules. Creature type alone grants no mental immunity. Actual mental/Enchantment/other defenses apply only within their written scope; immunity only to Charmed does not automatically block a spell that never imposes Charmed. No automatic cantrip scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30 feet/V,S and apparent healing with no actual healing effect. NEW: WIS save, fleeting relief and one-Perception-check distraction lasting one target round. The Healing tag supplies no healing trigger; the numeric distraction is an explicit reviewed addition.

operational.targets: One creature you perceive within 30 feet and line of effect; it need not already be concentrating or known to remember anything.
operational.duration: Instantaneous; the affected interval’s firsthand episodic recall is lost rather than temporarily suppressed.
operational.resolution: The target makes a Wisdom save against your spell DC. Success: no effect. Failure: remove its own episodic recollection of the six elapsed seconds immediately preceding this spell’s resolution, and end every actual Concentration application it is personally maintaining through each application’s normal ending procedure. No second concentration save is granted by this spell.
operational.effect: This changes recall, not the world or its state. Movement, attacks, damage, healing, deaths, conditions, resources, RP, Dissonance/Refrain, consumed uses, recorded choices, action budgets, physical evidence, other observers’ memories and completed outcomes stay as they occurred. The target can learn facts about that interval afterward from witnesses or evidence, creating new knowledge without restoring its erased firsthand memory. Each legal cast affects only its own resolution-relative six-second interval; overlaps never recursively reach older memories. A memory-only protection prevents only the memory change unless its scope also covers the concentration disruption; an empty remembered interval does not itself prevent ending actual concentration.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, duration, targets, uses or information.
operational.limitations: Multiple actual concentration records maintained by this target all end, including the linked pairs permitted by Spell Tether or Crimson Harmony. Tethered Cast’s separately sustained concentration spell is included despite not occupying the normal slot; its separate damage-save rule is not immunity to an effect expressly ending all maintained concentration. Unrelated sustained or permanent non-concentration effects, class features merely named focus, intrinsic traits and other creatures’ concentration do not end. Use actual ending consequences for held readied spells, summons, forms and fields; do not restore displaced effects or refund costs. Remembering the encounter poorly does not itself consume an Action, rewind a turn, clear a mechanically retained nonspell Ready record, create Unconsciousness or reset initiative. The spell supplies no replacement memory, information about what was erased, blanket forgetting of older associations, automatic notification of success, or immunity to later casts. Separate features that actually repair lost memories retain their own permissions. Actual class access, repertoire, components, costs, Dissonance/Refrain, beginning hooks, concentration transitions and counter windows follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Base 0 RP does not waive Action/components or Refrain. A failed, blocked or countered cast refunds no committed cost and restores no old concentration. V is audible and S needs its normal usable hand; subtle names do not hide casting. Saves use the actual casting class's spell DC, with ordinary binary save rules. Creature type alone grants no mental immunity. Actual mental/Enchantment/other defenses apply only within their written scope; immunity only to Charmed does not automatically block a spell that never imposes Charmed. No automatic cantrip scaling.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action/30 feet/V,S/instantaneous, forget the last six seconds and end concentration. NEW: WIS save, permanent resolution-relative episodic loss, all currently maintained Concentration scope and independent defense handling. Exact-class completion includes Spell Tether, Crimson Harmony and Tethered Cast under actual maintained-concentration rules; it does not alter their source cards.

Complete the current packet's split and life consequences before concentration failure caused by that packet ends the bond; never undo a committed share. One Warding Bond per participating creature across all casters; casting cannot create chains or cycles. Ordinary cover and walls after application do not block the sense. A specific divination/masking protection applies to its actual scope; a blocked read supplies no bearing. Beyond 1 mile or on another plane also gives no bearing, without distinguishing why. Shapechange, disguise and appearance changes retain the same creature identity and do not detach or transfer the mark. Death, destruction or the ending of the marked summon’s existence ends this application. It does not resume on revival, reconstruction or resummoning and does not track a corpse, detached soul or replacement body. A shapechange that retains the same continuing creature identity does not by itself count as death, destruction or an ended summoned existence.

operational.targets: Select one individually perceptible ongoing magical shield effect and designate one creature it currently protects. Both its legal effect-targeting locus and that creature must be perceived, within 30 feet and line of effect from you, at commitment and resolution. This spell grants no detection/identification ability or free owner/rank diagnostic. For a distributed Protective Sphere, use the explicit boundary/inside-creature procedure in Effect.
operational.duration: Instantaneous ending and subsequent damage, no concentration.
operational.resolution: After paid commitment, resolve actual hidden eligibility: spell origin, recorded generating rank 0–1, eligible protective identity, ongoing operational defense of the designated creature, and susceptibility to ending. Failure of any required predicate means no ending, no damage, no replacement target and no refund. If eligible, automatically end exactly that selected effect/component through its ordinary parent/dependency callbacks. Only after successful ending, deal one automatic1d8 force packet to the designated still-legal creature. No attack/save is added. If the effect cannot actually end, there is no damage fallback.
operational.effect: NEW eligible-shield definition: one individually perceptible ongoing magical effect generated by an actual rank-0 or rank-1 spell whose source expressly identifies or describes it as a shield, barrier, ward or unambiguous equivalent magical protective layer, and which currently retains at least one operational defensive component protecting the designated creature. Defensive components include attack/AC protection, damage prevention/reduction/absorption, projectile or creature interception, saving-throw protection, or an actual magical defensive boundary. A generic defensive benefit does not qualify without that source-qualified identity. Stronger same-stat numerical supersession does not end eligibility; actual complete suppression of every defensive component prevents eligibility until protection resumes. An active conditional defense need not currently be triggered. The actual generating rank controls, not RP spent, discount, dispeller level or a different class placement. Reviewed examples: Arcane Ward, active Shield, active Barrier Flicker, Corruption Ward and unconsumed Minor Elemental Ward qualify subject to all gates. Rank-1 Abjuration Alignment Shield qualifies without a currently attacking opposed-alignment creature; its rank-3 Conjuration application fails the rank ceiling. Resonance Shield qualifies only if its own accepted current temporary-HP grant has points remaining and has not expired/depleted/replaced. The reviewed finite source-owned grant is an ongoing effect despite old Instantaneous metadata; this does not make historical instantaneous consequences generically dispellable. Remove only that actual accepted grant administratively, never a discarded historical grant or a replacement False Life/class pool. Administrative removal is not damage, a hit or paid absorption and triggers depletion/removal hooks only where their actual wording covers it. For Protective Sphere, choose one perceived actual boundary point within 30 feet/line of effect as the effect locus, and one perceived creature actually inside it also within 30 feet/line of effect. That creature need not be the owner, and no projectile must be in flight. End the whole one selected maintained sphere application and its actual dependencies, not a hole or segment; overlapping independent spheres remain. An outside creature cannot be designated merely through hypothetical protection by the sphere.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, targets, duration, uses or magnitude.
operational.limitations: Generic temporary HP, generic resistance/save buffs, information-only wards, permanent magic, items, class engines, creature traits, ordinary physical shields and spell-created purely physical objects fail this predicate unless another exact rule expressly makes that source eligible. Saves use DC 8 + PB + actual casting modifier and binary-save rules. Actual target/area defenses and source-specific hooks retain their real trigger scopes. No automatic level scaling, generic upcast, new action budget or resource generation.

operational.targets: Choose a perceived point on an actual physical supporting surface within 30 feet and line of effect. Affect a10-foot-radius patch on ONE contiguous supporting surface associated with that center, with line of effect from the center. Initial creature targets are every creature actually standing on/physically supported by that eligible patch, including you/allies; no selective omission.
operational.duration: Instantaneous initial damage; difficult terrain up to one minute, no concentration. In initiative the maximum ends at the caster’s tenth future regular-turn START after application, excluding a start already underway/passed. Outside initiative it ends 60 elapsed seconds after application. Preserve the original regular/virtual marker or absolute deadline through initiative changes, extra turns, absence and travel; no timing-mode change resets the maximum.
operational.resolution: Each initially supported creature makes a Dexterity save. Roll3d6 bludgeoning once. Failure: full raw result; success: no damage; each creature’s actual defenses apply. Regardless of individual saves, the eligible patch becomes difficult terrain for its finite duration.
operational.effect: The patch is a magical movement-cost effect on existing ground, floor or platform, not permanent material alteration. Its source-defined support/line-of-effect topology does not propagate through walls, floors/ceilings to another storey, or onto disconnected/stacked platforms merely because they fit a3D radius. Air/open water supplies no qualifying supporting surface. A normal building floor can qualify without receiving structural damage. Moving through the patch uses ordinary difficult-terrain costs; flying creatures not using that surface do not incur its cost. Separate casts retain their own patches/deadlines, but identical overlapping difficult terrain does not multiply the cost.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic increase in damage, range, targets, duration, uses or magnitude.
operational.limitations: No recurring damage on later entry, Prone, structural cracking/collapse, excavation, rubble inventory, permanent terrain or physical difficult-terrain object survives ending. Expiry, actual removal or eligible dispelling ends the relevant magical patch; it neither rebuilds nor damages the real surface. Initial creature damage and the shared terrain effect are separate, so a successful save prevents only that creature’s initial damage. Initial area targets are a snapshot at resolution, with no selective omission or later entry damage. Each affected creature uses its own save/defenses; a shared raw damage roll is not a shared defensive result. No Burning, Frozen, Deafened, Poisoned or other unnamed condition arises merely from the damage type. Actual class/source access, repertoire, level, action availability, components, costs, concentration transitions, Dissonance/Refrain and cast/counter/outcome hooks follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. These actual rank-1 placements have base 2 RP; real source modifiers and strain surcharges still apply. V is audible, S requires the ordinary usable free hand or an actual exception, and F is the ordinary class focus. A legal cast commits payment and cast-begin consequences before its Counterspell window; later failure/countering refunds nothing and restores no displaced concentration. Spell attacks use d20 + PB + actual casting modifier against AC; natural 1 misses/natural 20 hits and doubles only actual attack damage dice. Saves use DC 8 + PB + actual casting modifier and binary-save rules. Actual target/area defenses and source-specific hooks retain their real trigger scopes. No automatic level scaling, generic upcast, new action budget or resource generation.

operational.scaling: None. Damage dice, target count, range and duration do not automatically increase with character or class level.

Conjured water cannot be sold, stockpiled beyond the one active batch, fermented into permanent commodities, or count as a permanent crafting/industrial ingredient. It provides ordinary hydration while it exists. Repeated cantrip casts use shared Refrain rules. Consuming or replacing batches never bypasses the once-per-recipient-per-24-hours hydration limit. Conjured water in a creature does not disappear harmfully. The limit is an explicit provisional expedition-economy guard.
operational.designNotes: Core V2 blocks and catalog summaries are preserved alongside this card. Components use the existing class focus where Core says F or M/F; this focus interpretation is provisional. Exact target eligibility, duration endpoints, saves where absent, concentration where unclear and anti-loop limits are provisional integration decisions. Core instantaneous creation is given a one-hour conjured-object lifetime and one active batch, plus once-per-recipient hydration, as explicit new test limits. Conference decision: hydration resets on elapsed24hours, independent of ability to complete a long rest.

operational.targets: One perceived nonmagical, key-operated mechanical lock within range and line of effect; conjure its key into your free hand. A free hand able to receive/use an ordinary key is required at creation.
operational.duration: If applied in initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; preserve that virtual source-start phase through initiative changes, departure or death. It can be handed to another creature and used normally for the duration, including locking or unlocking repeatedly if the actual mechanism and available interactions allow. It cannot operate another lock. Its vanishing does not retroactively undo the physical lock's resulting state.
operational.scaling: None.
operational.limitations: One Phantom Key per caster; a successful new application ends that caster's prior key. Ordinary hand, custody, carrying, access and object-interaction rules apply; a second interaction or a mechanism requiring an Action still costs that Action. It does not disable, detect or bypass traps, jams, barricades, combination/keyless locks or magical protections. A separable mundane physical mechanism on a magically warded lock can accept the key; the ward, including Arcane Lock, remains in force and requires its own permission or removal. A purely magical lock is ineligible. The key supplies no permanent key, harvestable/saleable material or automatic durable blueprint. Ordinary observations and deductions still work; no memory or inference is erased. A successful new application owns its own endpoint; stale expiration or consumption of an older application cannot remove its replacement. A countered new cast creates no replacement. Known/prepared access, class level, components, line of effect, cast costs, concentration transitions, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. Total cover blocks direct targeting and the originating spell's line of effect. No automatic level scaling.

The historical Instantaneous metadata is reconciled as creation followed by a finite temporary object. Thief Lockpick Mastery remains a separate +5 tool/check feature; the strong mundane-lock bypass is an explicit unresolved balance question, not silently rewritten into proficiency or advantage.

completeCurrentEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Wisdom is the Cleric class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Cleric levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Wisdom modifier) unless a feature explicitly substitutes another ability. Cleric technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier. Cleric technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier.

Conviction is separate from Resonance Points. Base Conviction maximum is 3, automatically becoming 5 at Cleric 9; after a long rest you begin at your current maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent Conviction, to the maximum. A completed long rest restores all Conviction. Conviction Pool raises the maximum by 2. Conviction persists between encounters; simply declaring prayer, repeating a Rite, or performing harmless actions outside a real encounter never generates Conviction.

Only explicit features generate Conviction. Sacred Chant, Sermon of Purpose, Doctrine Shield, Dark Conviction and other printed cards are valid generators. A feature cannot generate more Conviction than its text permits, and Conviction can never exceed the current maximum. Summoned creatures, friendly creatures, trivial creatures, repeated corpse manipulation and staged out-of-combat actions cannot be used to farm Conviction.

Cleric techniques use only their printed RP and Conviction costs. All RP is paid from the Cleric's Core Systems V 2 Resonance Point pool. A Cleric technique is not automatically an ordinary spell-rank cast and does not receive Overcast, spell-slot, cost-discount or spell-proc benefits unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Ordinary spells continue to use Core V 2 spellcasting rules.

Protected Dissonance interaction: once on each of your regular turns, when you spend at least 2 Conviction on a Rite or Invocation, reduce Dissonance by 1, minimum 0. The expenditure must actually occur; waived Conviction costs do not vent Dissonance. A single feature expenditure vents at most once even if it spends more than 2 Conviction. No Cleric card automatically adds Dissonance unless explicitly written.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect immediately ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; for this pilot, if a division requires rounding, half damage is rounded down. Sustained Cleric effects use their printed maintenance cost and Bonus Action. A control effect that persists for multiple pulses or rounds gives the target a new save at each printed pulse or at the end of each affected turn as stated.

Round recharge counters are set after resolution and decrease once at the start of the Cleric's regular initiative turn, even if the Cleric cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not create extra recharge ticks. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one recharge tick. Only a positive counter may be reset or shortened, and a named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

Healing cannot exceed maximum HP, does not remove Wounds, and does not restore a dead creature unless a card explicitly says it resurrects. No Cleric feature provides unlimited permanent HP or resource restoration outside encounters. Temporary HP does not stack with itself; use the higher value. Resurrection and corpse-based effects have explicit use limits and cannot generate repeatable corpses, XP, loot or Conviction.

Invocation Attunement is gained automatically at Cleric level 2. Choose exactly one Invocation Path: Radiance, Judgment, Renewal, Flame, Veil or Echoes. Only the selected path bonus becomes active. Divine Invocation uses the mode belonging to that selected path unless another feature explicitly permits a different mode. Changing Invocation Path requires a future explicit retraining rule; this draft provides none.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION FOR PLAYTEST. Cleric 1: gain the Divine Favor engine and choose 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Cleric 2: automatically gain Invocation Attunement and the selected Invocation Path bonus, then choose 2 additional Base cards. Cleric 3: enter Bishop and choose 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4-8 each grant one eligible Base/Arch choice, respecting each card's minimum class level. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus Bishop's Mandate automatically. Level 10 choose Saint, Priest or Cultist and gain 2 Hero choices from that path. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one additional Hero choice; levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. The chosen Hero Finale is automatic at Cleric 20. ASI/feat milestones remain separate and do not consume these choices.

All acquisition gates use Cleric class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus still follows normal total-character-level rules. A multiclass character cannot use non-Cleric levels to unlock Bishop, Hero, Invocation or Finale features. Divine commands, visions and social abilities can influence actions only to the extent their exact mechanical text states; no Cleric feature can force a player character to adopt, abandon or profess a belief.

Capacity clarification: the automatic level 9 Conviction increase is a new draft completion so every Hero can pay its 5-Conviction Finale without buying Conviction Pool. Conviction Pool adds 2 at any level, yielding 5 early or 7 from 9. It never fills gained capacity immediately.

completeCurrentEngine: Blood Gauge (BG) starts and ends each encounter at 0, capacity 3; Spill Control raises capacity 6 while known. Once on your own regular turn, a weapon attack that damages a hostile living creature grants 1 BG. Hemorrhage Slash uses this same trigger, not an additional one. Explicit critical/kill/refund features can add more, but total BG gained is capped 2 per round. Self-inflicted damage, allies, summons, helpless captives and repeated damage to a corpse never generate BG. Blood is an encounter resource, not a currency carried into rest.

Dexterity governs weapon attacks; Intelligence governs hemomancy save DC and M. S scales from Crimson Agent class level. A weapon technique includes only its printed attacks, with normal weapon die plus Dexterity (or Strength when that weapon requires it). No free attack is implied by attack-speed wording. Class BG and RP are separate. Once per turn when casting an ordinary spell, optionally spend 1 BG to prevent 1 of that cast's Dissonance gain, minimum 0; never reduce RP this way.

Your Bleed is a physical ongoing effect on a living, non-bloodless creature: 1d4 damage at the start of each of its next 3 turns, then ends. It is not a new attack and generates no BG or procs. Refresh duration instead of stacking; Blood Echo expressly allows two independent instances, maximum. An Action by the victim or an adjacent creature using a healer's kit ends all your Bleeds on that victim. Apply physical resistance/immunity normally. Track remaining ticks and creator per instance. Allied healing versions from Bloodweaver cost RP and never count as hostile Bleeds for detonation, spreading or generation.

One Blood Mark at a time on a living target with your Bleed, except Phantom Strike, which explicitly may apply the mark without Bleed. It does not add a free Bleed. Marks last 5 of your regular turns, expire on encounter end or if the target dies, and never create damage by themselves. Rupture requires the target still within 60 ft and line of effect; it spends the mark. A mark does not defeat cover, planar boundaries or bloodlessness. Bloodtrail has its own tracking limits.

Veinweaves are self buffs unless their card expressly allows an ally. They require concentration and one may be active. Crimson Harmony is an explicit exception permitting two Veinweaves as one linked concentration burden; a failed concentration check ends both. A non-Veinweave concentration effect replaces the whole group. BG is spent on activation; no upkeep unless printed. Damage-sharing is redirection before mitigation, not extra damage: apply each recipient's own defenses once and never redirect the redirected portion again.

The healing, execution and denial text below deliberately bounds the source's vague percentage/instant-kill claims. HP sacrificed is direct loss, bypasses temporary HP and defenses, cannot be redirected, and cannot reduce the donor below 1. Only a willing ally can donate. HP sacrifice is never damage for class triggers. No class feature here restores the dead or removes Wounds.

At level 1 learn the core Blood Gauge/Bleed rules automatically. Blood Mark and Veinweaver's Core remain selections; Quickblood can be selected and used without a second unlock tax. Veinweaver's Core improves that foundation as printed. Standard scheduled acquisition applies. Bloodbound Edge is automatic 9. At 10 choose Bloodweaver, Shadow Operative or Thirstborn; its Final Cut is automatic 20. Duplicate Hemostasis names are separate Arch and Bloodweaver IDs.

Capacity clarification: Blood Gauge automatically reaches capacity 6 at class 9. Spill Control allows reaching 6 early but never raises the cap above 6. This new explicit gate ensures a later 5-BG Final Cut can be used without an optional capacity selection. Gain cap 2/round and encounter reset 0 still apply.

completeCurrentEngine: Strength is the class ability. Momentum starts/ends encounters at 0; cap 5, rising to 7 with Momentum Overflow or automatically at class 9. On each regular turn, moving at least 15 ft under your own power grants 1 Momentum, and damaging an enemy with a weapon attack grants 1 more. These are the only default gains; all gains/refunds together cap 2 per round. Forced movement, teleportation, movement in place, allies and summons cannot farm Momentum. Movement counts actual path traveled toward a tactical destination; one threshold per turn.

A leap technique moves you through an unobstructed arc to a visible unoccupied landing space within its range, adjacent to its target when attacking. Land during the same activation. It spends movement equal to horizontal distance, unless the card expressly supplies additional movement. A leap never gives flight, indefinite airborne immunity or free attacks. You cannot leap through ceilings/walls; vertical height is at most half the printed horizontal range. Safe technique landings do not cause self-fall damage; interrupted/falling travel follows ordinary falling rules. No bonus damage is earned by repeatedly dropping from a ledge.

All attack cards use a wielded polearm unless they explicitly describe a non-weapon save effect. A technique is its own Action, not an Attack Action plus free technique. At class 5 your ordinary Attack Action makes two attacks, at most two even when multiclass features overlap; each technique still gives only printed attacks. This automatic Extra Attack is a new explicit advancement specification for the pilot.

Armor bypass means the exact printed attack bonus or resistance exception, never subtracting a percentage of the target's whole AC. Critical ranges do not stack. A Dragoon can use only one free/Bonus Action leap granted by class features per round; it cannot trigger another free leap. Extra full Actions share the suite-wide cap. Reaction intercepts require a legal path and destination and do not rewind resolved damage.

Spending Momentum pays before resolution; a hit refund cannot pay its own activation. Burn means 1d4 fire at start of target's next 2 turns, nonstacking. Bleed means 1d4 physical at start of next 2 turns; an Action with a healer's kit ends it. Do Ts give no Momentum or critical triggers. Hard denial uses the shared once-per-target/encounter guard.

When casting an ordinary spell after moving at least 20 ft this turn, reduce that cast's Dissonance gain by 1, minimum 0; no automatic RP discount. Dragoon techniques are martial unless their card specifies elemental magic. Use Core V 2 RP and the Dragoon rank gates for separate spellcasting.

Use scheduled Base/Arch/Hero choices. Skybound Assault, Momentum Engine and related passives improve the automatic engine rather than unlock basic movement or generation. Lancer's Apex is automatic 9; at 10 choose Dragon Guardian, Drake Rider or Dragon Tyrant. The corresponding Final Flight is automatic 20. Apex Assault is an active technique despite its source passive heading.

completeCurrentEngine: Wisdom governs spells, form attacks and class DC/M. Hit Die d8; book armor, weapons, saves and skills remain. Retain your own ability scores, HP, saves, proficiency and personality in all forms; form traits replace only the stated anatomy, movement and attacks. No additional monster stat block or separate beast HP pool. One natural attack per Attack Action unless a form explicitly states otherwise, attack PB+WIS, printed dice+WIS damage. Missing natural attack is 1d6 bludgeoning; default walking Speed 30 ft, normal AC, Medium size. Hawk is Tiny, Bear/Earth Warden/hero forms may be Large when space permits. Equipment melds and cannot be used while melded; magical numeric bonuses persist only if compatible with form anatomy and never duplicate armor.

This class follows its explicit book progression instead of the ordinary 25-choice template. Base 1 grants Druidic, spellcasting, all five Base forms and 2 shifts/long rest. Choose one of seven Circles at 2; its level 2 features are a Base-stage exception. Enter the chosen Circle Arch path at 3, gain its 6 feature, then Circle Hero forms at 10 and its 14 feature. Arch Forms unlock 11 despite the historical word Arch; these are forms, not a second promotion. At 11 attune up to 2 Arch forms during long rest. Base forms remain available at higher levels. All features below are automatic at their gate for the chosen Circle; no generic extra class-card choices are added.

Preparation: two cantrips at 1, three at 4, four at 10, plus explicit Circle bonuses. Prepare class level+WIS modifier ranked Druid spells (minimum 1) each long rest, rank limited by Druid spell-rank access, not merely by enough RP. Use approved operational spell entries and Core V 2 RP table/costs in the shared configuration. Book rank-times-two cost and imported spell-slot terminology are preserved as superseded alternatives for this pilot. Circle always-prepared spells do not count toward preparation and use ordinary RP/Dissonance. Rituals must have ritual tag, be prepared and take printed casting time plus 10 minutes; waive base RP only, never consumed materials or other costs. ASI/feat milestones 4/8/12/16/19 belong to general advancement and must not be granted twice.

Shifting: Bonus Action, one long-rest shift use, 10 minutes, early reversion Bonus Action. Reaching 0 HP or incapacitation ends form; excess damage stays on your own HP. Shift uses follow detailed book table:2 at 1, 3 at 4, 4 at 7, 5 at 10, 6 at 13, 7 at 16, 8 at 19. Supplemental runtime alternative 2/3/4/5/6 at 1/4/8/12/16 remains preserved. At 20 changing form is unlimited but does not refill finite form benefits. Speech unavailable in Base forms, available in Arch/Hero. No spellcasting in form until Beast Spells 18 except an explicit form permission. Maintaining an existing spell concentration is allowed, still only one concentration. Changing form spends a use and ends old form features/summons; it does not reset once/rest abilities.

Transformation reserves prevent unlimited replacement HP: at long rest record Buffer Reserve=2 L+M and Form Surge Reserve=PB. A form giving temporary HP draws that many from Buffer Reserve, up to remaining amount, with normal nonstacking; never real healing. A form special described once/transformation also spends 1 Form Surge and cannot be refreshed by resuming the form. Form Surge refills only long rest. Forms cannot grant free casts, RP or shift uses. Auras affect at most 3 enemies and once per enemy per round; retaliation once/round total; ongoing riders refresh, never stack. Entering a legal Shapeshift clears the Refrain counter and remembered repeated-spell name, as the protected source contract requires. It does not reduce accumulated Dissonance. Natural attacks do not clear Refrain.

Circle of the Land chooses one terrain at 2. Always-prepared spell pairs at 3/5/7/9 are exactly the source table lines 2662–2669, reproduced in source appendix; their source names resolve to existing approved spell entries before use. They do not bypass rank gates. For this pilot Circle spells are permitted exceptions to ordinary list membership, not newly authored variants. Moon Circle Forms CR table is historical external-stat language: use only these bounded forms, not arbitrary CR beasts. Early Moon benefit is +S damage on first form hit each turn. No imported monster multiattack, spellcasting or legendary actions.

Circle summary: Land preserves lore and recovery; Moon improves shifting; Storm controls lightning and wind; Thorns works poison and roots; Winterfang works cold; Rotshaper uses bounded swarms; Ashen Grove works fire and regrowth. Land/Thorns duplicate Blight Elk and Tanglemaw names are kept as separate source identities. Source auto-failed hostile saves in Master of Decay/Ash become once/turn-2 on one save, not unavoidable control. Stronger supplemental flavor riders are represented explicitly below or retained as unadopted alternatives in source provenance.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Mage class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Mage levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier) unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Mage spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Mage spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

Spellcasting and Resonance Pool are automatic class features, never selection taxes. Use the Mage maximum Resonance Point pool and ordinary spell-rank costs from authoritative Core Systems Known Descent V 2. All Mage card RP costs and ordinary spell RP costs come from that same pool. There are no spell slots. A long rest restores RP according to Core V 2; other existing recovery rules remain separate unless this pilot explicitly overrides them.

Named Mage cards tagged mage-spell, and the three Focus finishers are spells for Focus, Nuke Chain, Refrain, concentration, Counterspell and other spell-referencing mechanics. Their printed RP cost replaces an ordinary rank cost; do not charge both. Generic Overcast is disabled for these class-card spells during this pilot unless a card expressly enables it. They receive no extra class-level Burn or Dissonance simply for being card spells; ordinary Core V 2 spell-risk rules still apply where applicable.

Elemental Focus is gained automatically at Mage level 2. Choose Fire, Cold or Lightning and automatically gain the corresponding Focus card. Your selected Focus determines the element used by Elemental Bolt, Elemental Surge, your Focus finisher and other effects that refer to your chosen element. Unless Elemental Pivot or another explicit effect changes it, the choice is permanent in this draft.

NUKE CHAIN. Track your last three consecutive Focus-eligible spell casts. A Focus-eligible cast is a Mage or ordinary spell that deals your currently chosen Fire, Cold or Lightning damage type and is identified by a distinct spell or card name. A spell of another element or a non-elemental spell clears the chain. The last three eligible casts must have three different names. Repeating one chosen-element spell remains a legal cast but shifts the three-cast window and follows ordinary Refrain rules; repetition does not receive special protection from Dissonance.

When the third different named chosen-element spell in the current three-cast window resolves, complete the Nuke Chain, reduce Dissonance by 2 to a minimum of 0, and prime your selected Focus finisher until the end of your next regular Mage turn. Chain completion occurs whether targets hit or save, provided all three spells were legally cast and resolved. A finisher is not itself a chain-building spell. Using the finisher or allowing it to expire clears the chain and the primed state.

FOCUS FINISHERS. A primed Focus finisher is a Bonus Action Mage spell costing 2 RP and is usable once per completed Nuke Chain. Each finisher also has a 3-round recharge. A completed chain can prime a finisher whose recharge is still positive, but the primed use expires normally if the recharge does not become ready in time. Finisher recharge is subject to the universal positive-counter reset limit of once per ability per round.

RESONANCE SURGE. Once per short rest, when you begin casting a damaging Mage spell, you may spend 2 additional RP after validating the spell's normal cost. Add S d8 damage of one damage type already dealt by that spell to one of its damage rolls. Resonance Surge does not count as Overcast, does not independently alter Dissonance or Burn, does not create another spell cast, and does not advance the Nuke Chain separately.

Only one concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect ends the first. Damage prompts the current Core Systems concentration save; for this pilot any required half-damage rounding is down. Round recharge counters tick once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if incapacitated, and every uninterrupted 6 seconds outside initiative. Only positive counters may be shortened or reset and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions. Mage summons and companions do not receive independent damaging turns: all Mage-controlled conjured companions share one Companion Command per Mage regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one companion to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded companions may move to remain near you and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose control.

ELEMENTAL FAMILIAR. Conjure Elemental Familiar creates one familiar matching your current Focus; you may have only one elemental familiar. AC = 12 + PB; HP = 5 + Mage level + M; Speed 30 feet; Lightning familiar additionally has Fly 30 feet, Fire has resistance to fire, Cold has resistance to cold. It uses your saves and PB where required. Elemental Dart: ranged spell attack using your Mage spell attack, range 30 feet, hit S d4 damage of its element. It cannot generate RP, Dissonance, Focus casts, corpses, XP, loot or kill-trigger resources.

LICH COMPANION SYSTEM. A successful Lich transformation unlocks three unique bound elite companions: Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound. You can maintain at most one of each, maximum three total. They return at full HP after a completed long rest unless a campaign consequence expressly prevents it. A destroyed elite leaves no usable corpse and cannot generate XP, loot, RP, Nuke Chain credit, Soul Reservoir or kill-based resources. Soulbound Ritual can return one before a long rest.

BONEFLAYER. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 12 + 2 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Bone Shards: range 60 feet, your Mage spell attack, hit 2d6 + S necrotic. Fear Pulse: instead of Bone Shards, enemies of your choice within 10 feet make Wisdom saves against your Mage DC; failure causes Frightened until the end of their next turn; recharge 3 rounds. Grave Miasma: instead of Bone Shards, one 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet persists until the start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3 rounds.

DREADBLADE. Medium undead; AC 16; HP = 16 + 3 × Mage level; Speed 30 feet. Disrupting Blade: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. If the target is concentrating it immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20, the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 to attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

WRAITHBOUND. Medium undead; AC 14; HP = 10 + 2 × Mage level; Fly 40 feet and can hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn, it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: melee spell attack using your Mage attack bonus, reach 5 feet, hit 1d8 + S necrotic. On a natural 20, the target makes a Constitution save against your Mage DC; failure Stuns it until the end of its next turn.

LICH TRANSFORMATION READINESS. At Mage level 10 a character may select Lich only after obtaining either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants, binding at least two named mini-bosses as guardians, securing a planar nexus and surviving the Director's divine-echo encounter. A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check. If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.

Before the irreversible Lich roll, the Director must explicitly tell the player the historical failure stakes: permanent loss of spellcasting, transformation into a cursed melee undead NPC, hostile faction consequences, cursed-gear restriction and no further XP as that retired PC. The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Mage 1 automatically gains Spellcasting, Resonance Pool and Resonance Surge, then chooses 4 eligible selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Mage 2 automatically chooses and gains one Elemental Focus card, then chooses 2 additional Base cards. Mage 3 enters Arcanist and chooses 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4 through 9 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch card; level 9 is an ordinary choice because the historical source has no Arch capstone.

At Mage 10 choose Archmage, Elementalist or, if its ritual succeeds, Lich; choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. Mage 20 grants one additional Hero-path choice plus the NEW playtest level-20 class capstone in extra Cards. No historical Hero Finale is implied. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition gates use Mage class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus remains the normal total-character proficiency bonus. Non-Mage levels do not unlock Elemental Focus, Arcanist, Hero cards, Nuke Chain upgrades, Lich ritual access or the level-20 Mage capstone.

Class-spell ranks are printed in the normalized card data: use the legal maximum Mage rank at that card's minimum class level, capped 9; the three Focus finishers are rank 1. Rank determines Dissonance, Counterspell and rank-limited interactions, not a second RP cost. A shared spell uses the ally's normal Action and caster-side Dissonance at the moment it is cast; it never builds the Mage's Nuke Chain remotely. Spellcasting through Fracture as Lich uses the shared direct-trauma rule.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: Intelligence is the class ability; use d8 Hit Die from the detailed book, recording the older runtime d6 as superseded for this draft. You begin with 3 empty Echo Slots. Expansion II raises ordinary capacity 5; Sacred/Floating memory features may add one restricted slot, but total concurrent stored Echoes never exceeds 6. Slots are storage, not spell slots. Releasing normally empties that record. Rest restores RP, not spent Echoes. Starting a new encounter does not duplicate the archive.

Mirrorbind is an Action, once per encounter, against a creature within 60 ft whose eligible ability you saw resolve since the start of your previous turn. Target must have INT 6 or lower, not be a boss or possess unique/legendary status unless an encounter script explicitly permits copying. It makes WIS save versus class DC; failure captures one witnessed ability into an empty slot. No copying from allies, your companions, another copy, a corpse, a recharge-limited legendary power or an at-will source that itself restores resources. You can voluntarily erase a slot without an action on your turn, permanently losing its record.

Record source creature/name, witnessed ability, category, damage type, allowed rank, capture encounter and whether first release has occurred. For this pilot, capture copies the observed role into ONE bounded profile: Strike=one target 60 ft class spell attack S d8 observed damage type; Burst=up to 3 enemies in 10 ft radius within 30 ft DEX save S d6, half on success; Mend=one living ally 30 ft S d6+M HP; Ward=one ally 30 ft S d6+M temporary HP for 1 minute; Hindrance=one enemy 30 ft WIS save or Speed-10 ft and no Reactions until end its next turn. Choose only a profile actually expressed by the observed source; physical attack cannot become healing. Rank is max(1, ceil(source challenge rating/2)); if source lacks a rating the Director assigns a rank before the encounter, not after seeing a desirable ability. Rank cannot exceed your Mirrorsage learnable rank; no copying character levels from a creature. Damage/targets/control are capped by these profiles, not source boss dice.

Echo Release costs the Core V 2 RP cost of the recorded rank, minimum 2, consumes its record and counts as a spell for Dissonance and Refrain. Spell attack/DC use your own stats. First release of a newly captured record ignores Refrain addition only; base strain remains. Any preserved subsequent release uses ordinary repeated-spell strain. All released Echoes, pet replays, fusions and reflections share ONE release action per round; a specifically combined package counts once but pays for every component and has its printed damage cap. Copies cannot create resources or recursive Echoes.

One Mirror Beast OR Reflective Companion, never both. Mirror Beast uses standard companion stats, initially copies appearance only, and costs a Bonus Action to command. You may command it to make its normal attack OR originate your round's Echo Release from its position, paying RP and consuming the record normally; not both. You still supply an Action for release unless a feature specifically changes that action cost. A shifted appearance grants no extra actions/stats. Destroying/dismissing it grants no capture, corpse, XP or recovery. Charm Bind is 1/long rest, 3 rounds, concentration, INT 6-or-lower target WIS save and repeat at each turn end/when harmed by your side; never a player character or boss without explicit encounter permission. A charmed companion uses its own ordinary attack with damage capped at standard companion S d6; unique spells/powers remain unavailable.

Focus Point is a separate resource: when Mimicry Focus is known, receive 1 at encounter start, maximum 1, lost at encounter end. It can modify one Echo without generating another release, recapture or resource refund. No stacking damage doublings; use the printed modest die/range boost. Healing/support copies always consume RP and cannot restore RP or duplicate limited-use features.

Standard acquisition applies; baseline Mirrorbind, Echo Release and summon procedure become usable by selecting their cards. Echo Channeling and Mirrorcall are upgrades, not duplicate mandatory unlocks. The contradiction between source initial 3 slots and Expansion I 2→3 is reconciled as an archive-safety upgrade below. Perfect Reflection automatic 9, Hero choice 10, corresponding Final 20. The finale does not override copy eligibility or the shared release cap.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Dexterity is the Monk class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Monk levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Dexterity modifier). Monk technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier. Monk technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Dexterity modifier.

Ki Chain is a Monk-only resource from 0 to 5. Begin each real encounter at 0 Ki and clear Ki when the encounter ends or after 1 minute without a real encounter. Ki cannot be generated by sparring with willing creatures, attacking objects, repeatedly dodging harmless attacks, healing between encounters or other staged actions. Ki is separate from Resonance Points and Dissonance.

Normal Ki generation is capped at 2 Ki during your own regular turn and 1 Ki total from reactions or defensive events between the end of one regular turn and the start of your next. Explicit spending has no per-turn cap other than available Ki. A feature cannot raise Ki above 5. Incapacitation or Stunned resets Ki to 0; ordinary damage does not.

All Monks automatically know Tiger, Tortoise and Crane Stances at level 1. Only one core stance can be active at a time. While unarmored and not using a shield, you may switch to one known core stance on your own turn without an Action, at most once per round. The stance remains until changed, incapacitated or the encounter ends. The optional Stance Shift feature improves when that same once-per-round switch may occur; it does not create a second switch.

Unarmored Flow is automatic class identity rather than a selectable card. Wearing armor or using a shield suppresses the mechanical benefits printed on Tiger, Tortoise and Crane Stances, Unarmored Speed, Perfect Balance and Tortoise Discipline features unless a card explicitly says otherwise. Ki Chain itself and Monk techniques remain usable unless their card requires being unarmored.

Tiger, Tortoise and Crane Ki generation obey the global Ki-gain ceilings. Tiger can generate Ki from critical unarmed strikes. Tortoise can generate Ki from specified defensive successes. Crane provides mobility and support but does not create free out-of-combat healing. A single event can satisfy more than one generator, but total gain still cannot exceed the appropriate own-turn or off-turn ceiling.

MINOR WEAVE INTERFACE. Cards tagged weave are magical Monk techniques. If a tagged technique would add at least 1 Dissonance under the broader Weave rules, after validating all ordinary costs but before resolution you may spend 1 additional Ki to prevent that 1 Dissonance. This prevention Ki is separate from the card's printed Ki and RP costs. It cannot prevent more than 1 Dissonance from one technique and cannot reduce Dissonance already present.

All printed RP costs use the character's existing Resonance Point pool where applicable; Monk cards create no second RP pool. Ki never converts to RP unless a card explicitly says so. Generic spell-slot mechanics do not apply. Monk techniques are not ordinary spells unless their card expressly says otherwise.

STUN GUARD. A creature can be Stunned by your Monk features at most once per encounter. Mark it after the first Monk-caused Stunned condition successfully applies. If another of your Monk features would Stun that marked creature later in the same encounter, the creature still makes the required save; on failure it instead loses its Reaction until the end of its next turn. This guard is tracked separately for each Monk.

Temporary maximum-HP reductions caused by Monk features do not stack on the same creature; use the largest reduction from your Monk features. Maximum HP cannot be reduced below 1. Unless a card specifies an earlier end, the reduction lasts until the creature completes a short or long rest. Restoring maximum HP does not restore current HP. These effects are temporary combat trauma, not unstated permanent injuries.

Only one concentration effect may be maintained at a time. Starting another concentration effect ends the previous one. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; any required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Round recharge ticks once at the start of the Monk's regular initiative turn, including while incapacitated; extra Actions and extra turns never create additional ticks.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. A named ability can receive at most one positive-counter recharge reset or shortening per round. Only an ability whose current recharge counter is above 0 can be reset or shortened.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Monk 1 automatically gains Ki Flow, Unarmored Flow, all three core Stances and basic once-per-round stance switching, then chooses 4 Base cards, at least 2 Active. Monk 2 chooses 2 additional Base cards. Monk 3 enters Master and chooses 2 Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Levels 4 through 8 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Level 9 grants one eligible Arch choice and Martial Apex automatically.

Discipline Initiate is an optional Base selection. Choosing Tank does not grant five free Base abilities: it unlocks the four non-final Tortoise Discipline cards as additional Arch-selection options at their listed Monk levels. Final Form — Bastion of Breath is never a normal selection; at Monk 9 or the first later level when eligible it is gained automatically only if you chose Tank through Discipline Initiate and know at least three of Stone Shell Discipline, Redirecting Palm, Iron Shell Pulse and Echoing Guard. Tortoise Discipline remains compatible with any Hero path chosen later.

At Monk 10 choose Enlightened Master, Iron Fist Master or Way of Shadow and choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch card, including unlocked non-final Tortoise cards. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. At Monk 20 the chosen Hero path's Final is automatic and cannot be selected earlier. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition and scaling gates use Monk class level, not total character level. Normal character proficiency bonus still uses the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock Master, Tortoise Final Form, Hero features or a level-20 Final.

Healing from Monk cards cannot exceed maximum HP, restore the dead or remove Wounds unless explicitly stated. Permanent HP recovery and Ki generation cannot be farmed outside encounters. Resurrection effects are explicitly limited-use. No Monk card can instantly kill a target merely because a descriptive source used language such as Death Touch; death continues to follow the game's ordinary damage and dying rules.

Unarmored Flow completion: while wearing no armor or shield, AC=10+DEX modifier+WIS modifier, or ordinary armorless AC if higher, never both. Unarmed strikes use DEX for attack/damage and 1d6 at 1, 1d8 at 5, 1d10 at 11, 1d12 at 17. This is a new numeric completion; no automatic Extra Attack beyond printed techniques.

Each technique tagged weave creates 1 D in this pilot, unless it explicitly says otherwise. Ki can prevent up to 1 D before resolution only if remaining Ki pays that additional cost. Full-Ki capstones may legally accept D. The Stun Guard shares the suite-wide once/character/target hard-denial mark; its later failed-save fallback of reaction loss is an explicit Monk exception, not a second Stun.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Charisma is the Oracle class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Oracle levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Charisma modifier). Revelation attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier. Revelation save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier.

HIT DIE CONFLICT. The class overview registry lists d8, while the detailed Player Rulebook Oracle entry states 6 + Constitution modifier at level 1 and d6 per Oracle level thereafter. This pilot uses the detailed rulebook d6 chassis: 6 + Constitution modifier at Oracle 1 and 1d6 per later Oracle level. The d8 registry value remains a preserved alternative pending owner adjudication.

The Oracle is an exceptional progression class rather than a 25-choice Base/Arch/Hero class. Base Oracle is levels 1-2, Revelation Tier development is the Arch-stage progression at levels 3-9, and Revelation Mastery is the Hero-stage progression at levels 10-20. Mystery and Curse are chosen at level 1 but their later Revelations, Boons and Final abilities remain class-level gated.

Choose exactly ONE Mystery and exactly ONE Curse at Oracle level 1. They are not parallel subclasses that stack. You never gain another Mystery or Curse unless a future explicit retraining or transformation rule says otherwise. Curse limitations are permanent and cannot be removed by ordinary cleansing, curse removal, resurrection or rest.

REVELATION CHARGES are the Oracle's only class power resource. Oracles do not use Resonance Points, spell slots, Weave Dissonance, Overcast or ordinary spell-rank casting for Revelations. Revelation Charges are abbreviated RC. A Revelation card's printed RC cost is paid once before resolution. An illegal activation spends nothing.

RC CAP SCHEDULE for this provisional module: maximum 3 at Oracle levels 1-2, 4 at levels 3-5, 5 at levels 6-8, 6 at levels 9-10 and 7 at level 11+. Increasing the maximum does not automatically refill spent charges except where another feature explicitly says so.

RC RECOVERY. A completed long rest restores RC to maximum. A completed short rest restores 1 spent RC, never above maximum. Each Mystery has exactly one Prophecy Trigger. During a real encounter, your Prophecy Trigger can restore at most 1 RC per round and never above maximum. Trivial enemies, willing staged targets, summoned sacrifices, repeated corpse abuse, copied damage, copied healing and events generated solely to trigger recovery do not qualify.

A single event can satisfy only one Prophecy Trigger recovery for you even if several descriptions could apply. A Revelation repeated or copied by another feature does not independently trigger Prophecy recovery unless that feature explicitly says it counts as a new Revelation use. Restored charges never recursively trigger another recovery.

At Oracle level 11, the preserved registry draft additionally sets your starting RC when a real encounter begins to at least max(3, your Charisma modifier), capped by your current RC maximum. If you already have more RC, keep the higher current value. This encounter-start floor occurs once per encounter and cannot be triggered by staged initiative.

REVELATIONS are divine class techniques, not ordinary spells. Unless a Revelation explicitly says otherwise, magical silence does not prevent a purely mental Revelation, but a Revelation requiring speech, touch, visible symbolism or another listed component obeys that requirement. Revelations do not generate Dissonance and cannot be modified by spell-slot, RP, spell-rank discount or ordinary spell-proc mechanics.

One concentration effect may be maintained at a time unless a specific Oracle feature explicitly creates a narrow exception. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration procedure; if half-damage rounding is required in this pilot, round down. Sustained Revelation control effects grant repeat saves at the cadence printed on the Revelation.

HARD CONTROL GUARD. A creature can suffer at most one Oracle-caused full-turn denial such as Stunned, Paralyzed, Incapacitated by control, or loss of its full Action from your Oracle features per encounter. After that succeeds once, later Oracle effects from you that would fully deny its turn instead remove its Reaction and reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of its next turn after the required save fails.

ADDITIONAL ACTION GUARD. All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. An additional Action cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Features that say a creature acts out of turn use this same cap. Movement-only grants do not count as additional full Actions.

Healing from Oracle features cannot exceed maximum HP, resurrect the dead or remove Wounds unless a feature explicitly says so. Temporary HP never stack. Encounter-only regeneration and drain cannot be farmed outside meaningful combat. Corpse effects create no XP, loot, RC or repeatable corpse resources unless expressly stated.

Copied, echoed, repeated or redirected damage/healing uses only the explicitly copied numeric component. It cannot repeat RC recovery, Prophecy Triggers, action grants, conditions, passive triggers, resource restoration or another copy effect unless the copying feature explicitly says otherwise.

BASE PROGRESSION. At Oracle 1 choose Mystery and Curse; gain the RC engine, Channel Revelation, Prophetic Insight and Divine Sense. At Oracle 2 gain Curse Manifestation, Oracular Trance and Oracle's Burden. No Base feature-selection currency or Skill Points are used.

ARCH-STAGE PROGRESSION. Oracle 3: choose one Tier I Revelation from your Mystery and automatically gain Curse Boon I. Oracle 4: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 5: automatically gain Curse Boon II; any Mystery-specific level-5 feature recorded by the registry belongs to the Mystery module below and does not create an additional generic feature here. Oracle 6: choose one Tier II Revelation and gain Mystery Surge. Oracle 8: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 9: gain your Mystery's fixed Tier III Revelation.

HERO-STAGE PROGRESSION. Oracle 10: gain Curse Boon III and Grand Revelation Foreshadow. Oracle 11: RC cap reaches 7 and the preserved encounter-start RC floor becomes active. Oracle 12: gain the Mystery-specific Mystic Insight. Oracle 13: preserved registry draft grants a second Tier II Revelation; after each completed short rest choose which of your two Tier II Revelations is Attuned for features that specifically refer to an active Tier II option, though both remain known and usable. Oracle 14: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 15: gain Revelation Mastery and Curse Boon IV. Oracle 16: preserved Prophecy Trigger Mastery. Oracle 17: preserved Grand Revelation Foreshadow upgrade. Oracle 18: Prophetic Surge. Oracle 19: separate ASI or eligible feat. Oracle 20: gain the Mystery's Final Revelation and Curse Boon V.

REVELATION MASTERY at level 15 never grants a Revelation you do not know. Choose one mastery enhancement explicitly listed by your Mystery for a Revelation you know. If a listed mastery names a Revelation you did not select, that mastery option is unavailable. Mastery cannot reduce RC below 0, create additional Actions beyond the shared cap or remove repeat-save requirements unless its exact Mystery text says so.

PROPHECY AND DIVINATION never force player beliefs, future choices or confessions. Information features can provide truthful clues, likely outcomes, symbolic visions or current facts, but the Director is not required to reveal unknowable future player decisions. Effects that command or compel a player-controlled character preserve the player's choice of targets and prohibit self-harm, permanent allegiance changes and belief alteration.

CURSE MANIFESTATION provides a common operational intensification rather than ten different hidden sub-engines. When activated, your Curse becomes visibly or metaphysically dominant for 3 rounds: gain +1 on Revelation attacks and +1 to Revelation save DC, but take -1 AC and -1 on your own saving throws for the duration. Any Curse limitation that can normally be voluntarily suppressed cannot be suppressed during Manifestation.

CURSE BOONS are automatic at Oracle levels 3, 5, 10, 15 and 20 for your ONE selected Curse. You do not choose between Curse Boons and do not gain Boons from unselected Curses. Each Curse card below operationalizes all five Boon gates and its permanent limitations.

All class gates use Oracle class level, not total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. Non-Oracle levels do not raise RC maximum, unlock Curse Boons, Revelations, Mystic Insight, Revelation Mastery, Prophetic Surge or Final Revelation.

INTEGRATION PRECEDENCE. The source ceiling draft conflicts with the registry on short rests and extra Revelation activations. This pilot explicitly chooses 1 RC on a completed short rest and permits a second Revelation only through an expressly granted extra Action or double-cast feature, never more than two Revelation resolutions per round. The preserved ceiling alternative is no short-rest recovery and one activation per round; do not combine both configurations.

All combat-triggered RC refunds, including Prophecy, damage riders and Curse Boons, share ONE recovered RC per round. Rest recovery, encounter-start floor and explicitly limited Final refills are separate. A free, copied or refunded use cannot recursively trigger another recovery. Apply this global cap even if an individual card says its recovery is separate.

The shared Prophetic Surge and your Mystery-specific level-18 Prophecy are two descriptions/options of ONE long-rest use, not two charges. Framework cards such as Tier III, Mystic Insight, Mastery and Final Revelation unlock the named Mystery card and never grant duplicate uses. A level-5 registry Mystery label grants no extra unnamed ability.

Oracle zone default: choose at most three allies and three enemies for each pulse or aura benefit, fixed at activation unless the card names fewer. Persistent damaging/healing zones require concentration and at most three pulses. Pay 1 RC before each pulse after the first, or end the effect; once-per-long-rest Finals include their printed pulses in that limited use. One pulse can affect a creature only once per round. Passive personal resistance and a single-target temporary buff are not zones.

Revelation backlash is the local one-turn penalty of -1 to attacks and saves and -5 feet Speed, ending at the end of your next turn. It is not a level of the general Exhaustion condition. Wound Eater's missed-feeding Exhaustion remains the general condition.

Initiative adjustments change order beginning next round. They never produce or erase a regular turn in the current round; a creature still gets at most one regular turn each round. Ties use the original initiative order. Fixed encounter-start bonuses do not retroactively reorder an encounter.

Extra attacks and echoed damage use base weapon/spell dice before critical-hit extra dice. A redirected damage event cannot be reduced a second time, reflected again or generate RC. Charmed alone does not grant command of a creature's actions.

Oracle’s exceptional ASI/feat schedule is 4, 8, 14 and 19. It does not gain extra ASIs at 12 or 16 from the generic class schedule. The rejected five-milestone draft remains in superseded Playtest Overrides for traceability.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: Charisma governs Oath DC/M and divine technique attacks. Weapon attacks use their ordinary Strength/Dexterity ability. Hit Die d10; all armor, shields, simple and martial weapons. Paladin has no Conviction or Oracle Revelation Charges. Lay on Hands is its own pool, 5×Paladin level, fully restored only by long rest. Ordinary spells and printed Smite fuel use the same Paladin Core V 2 RP pool; healing points never convert to RP.

Base progression is explicit rather than the ordinary 25-card template: at 1 automatically gain Lay on Hands, Divine Sense, Martial Proficiency, Divine Strike, Protective Stance and Sacred Touch. At 2 gain Righteous Challenge, Bolstering Presence, Fighting Style and ordinary Paladin spell access. At 3 swear ONE of ten Oaths; gain only its Smite modification, Aura and first Revelation spell. This Oath is the Arch specialization. At 10 enter Hero Oath Mastery of that SAME Oath; no second Oath or additional generic Hero tree. Signature Power unlocks 11, Final Gift 20. Oath Revelations automatically unlock 3/5/9/13/17, always known in addition to the shared spell repertoire, rank 1/2/3/4/5 respectively. Exact printed RP costs replace generic cost only if the card explicitly supplies them.

At 2 choose one Fighting Style: Defense +1 AC while armored; Dueling +2 damage to first one-handed melee hit on your own turn; Protection Reaction impose disadvantage on one attack against an adjacent ally when using a shield. At 3 Divine Health gives advantage on disease saves, not universal immunity. At 5 Extra Attack makes two attacks when taking the ordinary Attack Action; named attack techniques use their own counts. These three features reconcile preserved main-registry entries; other old level-table extras, including extra level 14 ASI and undefined free slot riders, are not stacked into this draft. ASI/feat at 4/8/12/16/19 follows general advancement once.

Divine Strike at 1: after one melee weapon hit on your regular turn, spend 1 RP to add S d6 radiant. At 2 this becomes Divine Smite: choose 1 RP for S d6 or 2 RP for(S+1)d8 radiant, once/own turn total. Oath 3 changes type/rider as its card states, never adds another copy of the base damage. Smite is not an ordinary spell, cannot be counterspelled or generically Overcast, and causes no Dissonance. A critical hit doubles Smite damage dice under ordinary rules, but never healing, resources or percentage copies.

One Oath aura, requires consciousness and no concentration. Radius 10 ft at 3, 15 ft at 6, 20 ft at 10, 30 ft at 15. Benefits affect up to 3 allies or 3 enemies as the Oath card states, chosen at start of your turn and changed next turn; they must stay within aura. At 6 choose one additional aura benefit for that day: allies+1 saves against fear/charm, or 1 flat DR against weapon damage. At 7 once/short rest when enemy damages an ally in aura, Reaction make one melee attack if in reach; may pay normal Smite cost even off turn, but total Smite maximum one per round from this reactive feature. At 10 aura persists until start of your next regular turn after incapacitation; then ends if still incapacitated. At 15 also grant selected allies+1 initiative while in aura when initiative is rolled; no retroactive turn changes.

At 17 Aura Surge once/short rest Bonus Action: until start next turn choose up to 3 allies in aura to gain S+M temporary HP and+1 saves. This bounded surge replaces vague doubling of every aura number. At 20 Divine Manifestation makes the aura active upon initiative without an action, radius 30 ft; it ignores ordinary Silence and terrain obstruction between allies but not antimagic explicitly suppressing divine powers, planar barriers or the consciousness rule. Source cannot-be-suppressed language is bounded explicitly. It grants no free Signature, Smite or Revelation spell.

Protected interface: Smite, Aura and Lay on Hands generate no Weave Dissonance. After a successful direct melee hit, your next Oath spell before end next turn generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0, consuming the benefit. No stacking, RP discount or Refrain reset.
