Oath Revelation spells and the five replacement Forbidden spells below are ordinary spells for strain, countering and concentration; signature powers and final gifts are Oath techniques unless expressly tagged otherwise.

Oath conduct clauses remain intact in source and Oath cards. The Director identifies a relevant clause and a knowingly chosen serious breach before applying a fall. A disagreement, failed roll, coerced act or unknown fact does not silently remove a character. A fall is an explicit story transition recorded with the player: choose the corresponding Oathbreaker inversion or pursue an agreed restoration scene. Preserve class level and already spent resources. Oathbreaker replaces its Oath Aura, Smite rider, Signature and Revelation list, rather than stacking both sets. Base martial abilities remain; Lay on Hands becomes Death Touch using the same current 5 L pool, with no refill on switching.

Death Touch baseline: Action melee divine attack PB+CHA; declare and spend 1 through 2 S+M points before the attack from remaining Lay on Hands pool to deal that much necrotic damage (choose amount before roll; miss still spends declared points). Each Oath inversion may alter type or add its bounded rider; never copy innate traits, confiscate class engines or automatically execute a target. A listed inverted Signature is available only at 11 and replaces the ordinary Signature use, one/short rest. An inverted aura follows the same radius, target cap and timing. Oathbreaker 20 uses the new Black Manifestation common capstone instead of its original Final Gift.

The source names a Forbidden Spell List but does not supply five complete entries for each inversion. This pilot explicitly adds one shared five-spell replacement list (below), with each Oathbreaker using its inversion name as flavor. These are new test rules, not recovered historical spells. Choose the normal Oath package OR inverted package at a time. All later Oath prerequisites still use Paladin class level; the Oathbreaker label does not bypass 3/11/20 gates.

Oath integration limits: one paid Smite total per round, including the level-7 Reaction; one Oath-aura reactive event per round. Multiple damage-redirection options share one event per round unless Crown Undying expressly allows two. Apply original-target defenses once, then split actual damage; transferred damage cannot be mitigated again, reflected, redirected again or generate resources. This explicit rule supersedes wording that permits recipient defenses again.

Sustained Oath spell damage/healing zones use concentration, at most three pulses, and 1 RP upkeep after the first pulse unless a priced card expressly supplies a different finite cadence. Native Oath auras retain their printed passive cadence and target cap. Final auras last their stated finite duration and include their pulses. All hard-denial effects, including compelled Actions, share the common once/source/target/encounter guard; later failures only remove Reactions and reduce Speed by half for one turn.

An emergency Reaction whose trigger itself incapacitates you, such as Grace Reversal or Thorn Crown, may resolve before that incapacitation only if you had a Reaction available before the triggering event. This grants no other actions while incapacitated. Narrative labels such as oppressor require a specific act of captivity/coercion established in the scene, not an alignment or identity assumption.

The source ceiling’s half-pool-per-round Lay on Hands cap is a preserved alternative. This pilot instead uses maximum class level per ordinary Lay on Hands Action and the explicitly once-per-long-rest level-17 Wave that distributes the current remaining pool. No normal heal gains the Wave’s exception.

For any one damage event choose exactly one Paladin redirection feature. Using it consumes the shared redirection allowance for that round. Crown Undying permits two DIFFERENT ally-damage events per round, but still only one redirection feature may modify each event.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: Dexterity governs weapons; Wisdom governs primal technique DC/M. This draft uses the detailed book's d8 Hit Die; older runtime d10 remains preserved as a conflicting alternative. At 1 gain Track Target engine: Bonus Action mark one perceived enemy within 90 ft for 1 minute, no RP, one quarry at a time; new mark replaces old. Once/own turn a weapon hit against quarry adds S damage. Mark does not reveal creatures through total cover. Track Target selection is an upgrade, not a second unlock tax.

Weapon Synergy tracks last successful direct weapon hit on your own turns. Changing melee→ranged grants+1 to that ranged attack roll if it is your first attack of the turn; changing ranged→melee makes the hit apply Bleed 1d4 on target's next 2 turns. Once/turn synergy; Do Ts, copies, companions, forced attacks and misses do not advance it. At 5 ordinary Attack Action makes two attacks; techniques use only printed counts. You may draw/stow one weapon as normal object interaction; Dual Style later improves this.

Elemental Attunement is defensive; Elemental Imbue is the separate Pathfinder feature gated 6. Imbue Bonus Action 2 RP, one element for 3 of your turns; once/turn a weapon hit adds 1d4 of chosen element plus fire:Burn 1d4 next target turn, cold:Speed-10 ft until end next turn, poison:CON save or-1 attack rolls until end next turn. Nonstacking; Do Ts never build Hit Chain. Switching element pays again.

Druidic Arrow Combo starts at Ranger 11, not at Base 1. Each direct successful weapon hit adds 1 Hit Chain, maximum 2 gained per regular turn and cap 3. Completing 3 primes one Arrow until end next turn; using it consumes the chain, even on miss. Efficient Killer lowers threshold 2. Chain starts/ends encounters 0, cannot be stocked against allies/captives/summons and is cleared by incapacitation. The Arrow is one Action with a ranged weapon attack or the stated save, costs 0 RP when primed, and is a magical class technique rather than an ordinary spell cast. At most one Arrow per round; it cannot advance its own chain. It requires a wielded bow and ammunition. Ordinary attack/damage riders apply once as printed, never another free arrow.

All Rangers learn five bounded Arrows at 11. Emberroot requires the previous 3 successful weapon hits carried fire imbue: ranged attack, weapon+S d6 fire on hit; up to 2 others within 5 ft take S fire, and primary target Burns 1d4 next turn. Glacial Thorn requires 2 ranged+1 melee among those 3 hits: ranged attack weapon+S d6 cold; on hit STR save or Speed 0 until end next turn. Venomlash requires poisoned/blighted terrain at you or target: ranged attack weapon+S d6 poison; on hit CON save or-1 damage on its next attack. Spirit Fang requires quarry: ranged attack at advantage, weapon+S d6 force; ignores resistance but not immunity on the added force only. Cleansing Grove requires natural terrain at you or target: up to 3 living allies within 10 ft of a point within 60 ft each end Frightened or Poisoned; no attack or damage.

Chosen Hero grants a sixth Arrow at 11. Warder Nature's Wrath: ranged attack weapon+S d6 piercing; up to 2 allies within 10 ft gain M temporary HP (finite mitigation, not repeatable real healing). Stalker Phantom: two ranged attacks against different aligned targets within 60 ft, each weapon damage, no extra dice; one Arrow activation. Outrider Corruption: place 10 ft-radius zone within 60 ft, concentration until start next turn; up to 3 enemies entering/starting there take S d4 necrotic once each, CON half. Arrow copies cannot generate extra attacks, resources or permanent terrain changes.

A successful direct weapon hit between ordinary spell casts clears Refrain and gives the next ordinary spell before end next turn 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0. The benefit is single-use/nonstacking; it reduces neither RP nor both base and repeat separately. Ordinary spells use Ranger rank gates and the shared test magic configuration.

Base choices 1–2, Pathfinder Arch 3–9, and chosen Warder/Stalker/Outrider Hero 10–20 are distinct stages. No source Arch capstone/Finale exists: level 9 receives its normal eligible choice, while 20 automatically improves your Hero Arrow once/long rest (new capstone below). Do not acquire a Hero by spending Base choices. Beast Companion is one permanent bond; it must be a willing/tamed noncorrupted beast with INT<7 and CR no greater than your class level. Its combat profile uses the bounded companion below rather than importing a full CR 20 monster.

If a primed Arrow expires unused, the prime ends and Hit Chain resets to 0. This applies equally to Efficient Killer’s threshold of two. Efficient Killer itself requires Ranger 11, when Hit Chain exists.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: Wisdom is the class ability. Choose Elemental Affinity automatically at 1: Fire, Ice, Air or Earth. Spellcasting/RP remain separate from Totem objects and flasks. Totem capacity 1, rises 2 at 13; any third replaces one of your existing totems. A totem is a visible Tiny magical object: AC 12+PB, HP 2 L, immobile, immune to poison/psychic/conditions, vulnerable to ordinary weapon and other damage. At 0 HP its aura ends. A new totem appears within 30 ft; cannot occupy a creature's space, serve as a bridge, trap a creature without a save or move through walls.

Totem Casting is Action 2 RP, duration 3 of your turns, 15 ft aura. Choose Flame, Stone, Frost, Spirit or Renewal. Benefits require an ally/target in the aura, maximum 3 creatures benefiting per pulse/round chosen by you. Flame adds 1 fire to an ally's first direct weapon hit per round; on critical that target Burns 1d4 next turn. Stone reduces damage by 1 and gives enemies-1 to STR checks to shove. Frost: enemy first entering/starting each round makes CON save or Speed-10 ft until end its turn. Spirit: first necrotic/hex damage per target per round adds 1. Renewal: on start and each of next 2 turns with Bonus Action+1 RP maintenance, up to 3 allies regain 2 HP. Thus Renewal total cost 4 RP for 3 pulses; no free healing on entry. All totems share one concentration burden; losing it ends all. Other concentration effects replace them. Non-Renewal auras need no Bonus Action upkeep. Multiple same-name/stat auras do not stack.

On your turn you may spend Bonus Action to move one totem up to 15 ft along unobstructed ground, remaining within 60 ft. This competes with healing maintenance, companion commands and advanced flasks. Moving an aura over a creature cannot trigger its once/round effect repeatedly. Totem destruction creates no resource return. Once per round, the first ordinary spell cast while inside your own active totem aura generates 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0; no RP reduction.

The book places Flask Use at Base but describes advanced flask casting as Theurgist/Soothsayer-only. For this draft, Base Flask Use grants mundane prepared tactical flasks thrown with an Action; at Hero 10 only Theurgist/Soothsayer gain magical Bonus Action flasks. Bloodcaller retains mundane alchemical knowledge, not the advanced flask subsystem. At long rest prepare 2 flasks, rising to 3 at 5 and 4 at 11; no encounter refill or stockpiling, total carry cap 4, unused contents become inert when preparing a new batch. This finite-rest supply replaces encounter-based free heal farming.

Flask tier uses S. Mundane Base modes: Burn=one enemy 30 ft DEX save S d6 fire half, failure 1d4 fire next turn; Root=one ground enemy 30 ft STR save Speed 0 until end its next turn; Weaken=one enemy 30 ft CON save or-1 attack damage until end its next turn. Advanced Hero modes additionally: Stun=one enemy 30 ft CON save or no Reactions, failure by 10 Stunned until end its next turn; Heal=one living ally 30 ft S d6+M HP; Restore=end Frightened or Poisoned on one ally 30 ft. Every thrown flask consumes one prepared unit and 2 RP for advanced magic (Base mundane flasks cost 0 RP). Changing payload requires no separate crafting action when throwing. No flask leaves harvestable poison or another flask.

Choose Fire/Ice/Air/Earth bonuses through affinity card; Ember/Cold/Shock damage are fire/cold/lightning, Earth uses bludgeoning. Summoned elemental spirits use one standard companion each, maximum one normally; Elemental Chorus expressly summons a package of 4 but all share one Bonus Action command and a printed combined pulse. Companions cannot generate RP, trigger flask refunds or create corpse/kill farms.

Bloodcaller at Hero 10 transforms permanently into Hagraven, with the player choosing this class path and its stated loss of ordinary Shaman spellcasting. It does NOT lose its RP reservoir: printed Hagraven/Totem techniques still pay RP, but it cannot cast ordinary Shaman spells or advanced magical flasks. It retains prior totem/technique selections. The change is a class choice, not permission for involuntary player-character conversion; ancestry identity and player control remain. At long rest it can prepare mundane flasks only if Base Flask Use is known.

Shaman Base 1–2, Spiritwalker Arch 3–9, and Theurgist/Soothsayer/Bloodcaller Hero 10–20 remain separate stages. Elemental Affinity is automatic 1, not an extra selection cost. No explicit Arch capstone in source:9 has its ordinary choice. At 20 your selected Hero's last active ultimate gains the explicit new capstone improvement below; no new generic Hero class is invented.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: A martial class with d10 Hit Die, all armor and shields, repeating crossbows, sidearms and siege tools. Dexterity governs ranged attacks; Constitution governs class DC/M and defensive techniques. No RP, ordinary spellcasting, Refrain or Dissonance engine. Names such as Divine Lockdown describe disciplined suppression; they do not grant divine magic.

Overwatch is an automatic Base engine at 1. Bonus Action designate a visible 15 ft square within weapon range until start next regular turn. Once during that interval, spend your Reaction when a perceived enemy enters, moves inside, attacks an ally from, or reveals itself inside the zone. Make one legal ranged attack with ammunition and line of fire, normally 1d8+DEX piercing. On hit choose Snare (Speed-10 ft until end next turn), Bleed (1d4 at start next turn), or Push 5 ft (STR save negates push). Concealment still applies. Only one Overwatch zone; no extra Reaction. The optional Overwatch card upgrades this engine. At 17 you may move 5 ft without opportunity attacks after its shot, once/round.

At 5 automatically gain Palisade Deployment. Spend one carried barricade kit and an Action to erect a 2-by 1-tile wall in contiguous unoccupied ground within 5 ft. Height 5 ft, AC 12, HP 5+CON modifier minimum 1, immunity psychic/poison; blocks movement and line of sight across its full height but can be climbed using 10 ft movement. One kit/use per encounter, two at 13; a long rest with carpentry tools replenishes 2 kits (carried maximum 2, reusable parts have no resale value). Material is required; no conjuring. At most one intact wall, two at 13. Old wall must be dismantled in 1 minute before replacement beyond cap. Once per encounter an Action repairs a wall for M HP using spare parts; destruction does not refresh uses.

Palisade Tier II at 13 doubles wall HP and grants resistance to damage from area effects. Hold Position: while adjacent to your intact wall gain+1 AC and+1 saves. Brace Line: an ally immediately behind you relative to a ranged attacker, with your wall adjacent to both of you, has 2 flat DR against that attacker. These bonuses do not stack with another Soldier wall; strongest flat DR applies. Full cover prevents attacks rather than granting an additional AC bonus.

Base 1–2, Commander Arch 3–9, then Champion/Artillerist/Tyrant Hero 10–20. Palisade 5 is automatic; Intercepting Shot has minimum 6 and Fortify Zone 9. Other cards require selection. There is no source automatic Arch capstone. At 20 gain the new Final Command below, clearly a playtest addition. No spell or sustained technique may be used to obtain infinite ammunition, structures, actions or permanent healing.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: Dexterity governs weapons and class DC/M. Choose Intelligence or Wisdom for noncombat class tool/sense checks at 1. Hit Die d8; light armor, daggers, shortswords, thrown weapons and hand crossbows; thieves tools and poison kit. Sneak Attack is automatic at 1: once on your regular turn, add ceil(class level/2)d6 to one finesse/ranged weapon hit if you had advantage, an active ally threatens target within 5 ft, or target is suffering your Bleed/Poisoned/Crippled. Disadvantage prevents Sneak Attack even if canceled into a straight roll. A feature can explicitly grant Sneak Attack on a different qualifying hit but never more than once/regular turn. Copies, poison ticks and companions cannot Sneak Attack.

Prepare fictional poison doses with poison kit during a long rest: maximum 3 carried at 1, 4 at 10, 5 at 15, 6 at 20; refill to this cap, never stockpile or sell these class preparations. A destroyed/confiscated kit prevents preparation until replaced. One dose coats one melee weapon or 2 projectiles, lasts 1 minute or until 2 attack attempts; hit applies its effect, miss still spends an attempt. Apply Poison card improves Action coating to Bonus Action; baseline coating is Action. Do not coat the same weapon with multiple doses except Double Poison. Fictional reagents come from ordinary adventuring supplies; no real-world recipes. Creating an exotic source-approved recipe requires an adventure specimen and one successful INT+PB poison-kit check DC 15, one attempt per specimen. It replaces a known recipe, not unlimited extra doses.

At 1 know all four Tier I recipes, at 7 add Tier II, at 14 Tier III. Poison saving throws use Thief DC except preserved source fixed DC 12 becomes max(12, Thief DC) for Mindburn/Venombite. Unless stated damage/conditions require a failed CON save; initial weapon damage is unaffected. Critical riders also need this failed save. One ongoing instance of each recipe per target; another application refreshes rather than stacks. Maximum 2 simultaneous different poison recipes from you per target. Bleed never stops all healing by default, Poisoned uses the Core V 2 condition: disadvantage on attacks and ability checks (not saving throws), and Shaken means disadvantage on next fear save. Neither is a hidden full-turn disable.

Tier I: Bloodleech gives Bleed 1d4 at start next 2 target turns; critical restores 1d4 of your HP, once per dose. Crippler gives-1 on next attack before end next turn; critical also half Speed for that duration. Mindburn uses WIS save: -1 spell-attack rolls until end next turn, critical also no Reactions. Venombite gives Poisoned until end next turn; critical also-1 on next save. Tier II: Ashblood adds 2d6 poison now and 1 fire at start next 2 turns; critical prevents HP recovery through end next turn. Silencer prevents verbal spellcasting through end next turn, critical also drops one held nonbonded item into its space; it can retrieve normally. Shiver gives Shaken through end next turn; critical also no Reactions. Hexroot gives-1 saves for 2 target turns; critical lets next weapon hit ignore resistance, never immunity, before end next turn.

Tier III: Voidspine deals 1d6 necrotic at start next 3 turns; critical adds-1 CON saves until end next turn, never changes ability scores/derived HP. Gravepetal makes target Unconscious until damage or end next turn, subject to shared hard-denial guard; critical also Prone and 3d6 poison immediate (resolve damage before unconsciousness). Neuroshock gives disadvantage on next DEX or WIS save before end next turn; critical also no Reactions. Wraithbane suppresses one observed bonus to AC (maximum 2) or damage resistance chosen before save until end next turn; critical prevents voluntary ethereal movement for duration. No core-engine, legendary action or creature-type removal; unsupported traits cannot be targeted.

Ordinary magical Thief techniques use the provisional minor-Weave RP pool and incur 1 D on use unless an ordinary spell says otherwise. Once per round, a Weave trick cast while hidden ignores its first point of Refrain Dissonance, as the protected source contract requires. It does not reduce base Dissonance or refund RP; a technique producing only its fixed 1 D receives no Refrain reduction unless it actually incurred Refrain. Arcane Trickster is still a Thief Hero, not an unrestricted full caster. Base 1–2, Rake Arch 3–9, chosen Arcane Trickster/Shadowblade/Blackguard Hero 10–20. Preserve advanced Arch gates: Distraction Tactics 13 and Crippling Strike 15 remain Arch selections obtainable after entering Hero. There is no automatic source Arch capstone; level 9 has its normal selection. Unseen Hand is Blackguard 20 automatic; the other paths receive the new level 20 finale below.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: Intelligence governs class DC/M, device attacks use PB+INT; Dexterity governs personal ranged weapons. Hit Die d8, light armor, shortbows/crossbows/simple weapons, tinkers tools and alchemist supplies. Technology is fictional equipment. Ordinary Tinker spells use RP/Dissonance; mundane bombs/devices with printed RP fuel costs are class techniques and do not separately count as spell casts.

At 1 automatically own one Anacite Drone: AC 13+INT modifier, HP 5+INT modifier+class level (minimum 1), flight 30 ft, ranged bolt 60 ft attack PB+INT for 1d6 piercing. Bonus Action commands one move and one attack or named module action; otherwise it Dodges and may follow you. On bolt hit roll d4; on 4 target CON save or cannot take Reactions through end next turn (Shock, no automatic Stun). All drones/turrets/scraplings share ONE damaging action per Bonus Action command per regular turn unless a card explicitly supplies a priced extra attack. No autonomous barrage. Drone is a construct, not immune to all conditions; poison/psychic immunity, no charm. Carry/retract it in 1 minute; no pocket extra world or passenger flight.

A destroyed drone remains 0 HP until repaired for 1 RP and 10 minutes with tools to half HP, once/short rest, or rebuilt during long rest to full. Ordinary repairing does not recharge devices, grant organic healing or trigger destruction bonuses. At 13 Dual Drone Protocols automatically chooses on each long rest either 2 basic drones each with one module, or one drone with 2 distinct modules. Still one command budget. Never more than 2 drones.

At 5 automatically gain one module slot; change module during long rest. Offensive: Burn Injector first bolt hit/turn causes 1d4 fire next 2 target turns; Poison Vents d4=4 on hit CON save or-1 attack rolls until end next turn; Concussive Bolt d4=4 on hit CON save or Stunned until end next turn, once/target/encounter shared denial guard and 1/short-rest successful Stun. Defensive: Target Taunter command action once/encounter WIS save one foe 30 ft or disadvantage attacking others until end next turn; Energy Shield command gives adjacent ally+2 AC until start next turn; Smoke Cloud command once/encounter creates 5 ft radius opaque smoke centered drone until start next turn. Support: Ammo Dispenser adjacent allies first ranged hit/turn+1 damage; Target Scanner command mark 1 visible foe 60 ft first ally attack before start next turn+1 hit; Tether Grappler command once/encounter pulls 1 willing ally 15 ft within 30 ft without opportunity attacks along open route.

Bomb stock refills during long rest with tools to 3 at 1, 4 at 5, 5 at 11; cap equals refill, class bombs have no resale or stockpiling. Encounter throw cap 1 at 1, 2 at 5, 3 at 11. Each throw uses one stock and one encounter allowance. Basic fire/cold known 1; advanced profiles known 6; Overload Core known 9. Base throw is Action, range 30 ft, 10 ft radius up to 3 creatures, DEX save S d6 element, half success. Fire failure adds 1d4 Burn next turn; cold failure Speed-10 ft until end next turn. Explosive Handling makes throw Bonus Action; still only one bomb/regular turn. At 15 Danger Close automatically allows excluding yourself/allies. Safe Detonation grants this early. Bombs cannot critically hit or inherit weapon riders.

Advanced bomb profiles replace basic rider: Thermobaric fire pushes 5 ft on failed STR save after damage; Cryo cold on failed DEX also Speed 0 until end next turn and d2=2 ignores 1 flat DR against this bomb; Shock lightning CON instead DEX, failure prevents verbal spellcasting until end next turn (construct instead loses Reactions), shared hard-denial guard; Glue no damage, 15 ft square difficult terrain 3 rounds and entering/starting DEX save or Speed-15 ft until end turn, once per creature/round. Overload Core destroys one commanded drone within 30 ft as part Action bomb, DEX save 2d6 lightning and no Reactions until end next turn on failure, half damage on success. Consumes stock/allowance; no further destruction proc.

Deployable slots start 1 at 6, 2 at 13, 3 at 17, separate from drone cap. Deploy Action 2 RP within 15 ft, fixed ground, AC 12+PB HP 2 L, duration 3 rounds, concentration not required; destroyed do not refund fuel. All share command budget. Sentry and Net require their cards. Additional engine profiles unlocked 6: Rocket Tower commanded attack 60 ft target DEX save S d6 fire/half success to up to 2 creatures within 5 ft, maximum 3 shots; Decoy Dummy one foe 30 ft WIS save when deployed or disadvantage on next attack against others, destruction S fire to one adjacent enemy no chain; Blast Wall 10-by 5 ft blocks LOS and movement, climb cost 10 ft. Net Trap one enemy entry STR save or Restrained, end turn repeat/Action escape DC, 3 round max then ends. One only fires when commanded except nonattack trap/decoy trigger; command budget limits damaging triggers too.

Base 1–2, Mechanist Arch 3–9, then Artificer/Techsmith/Warmachine Hero 10–20. Upgrade Slot 5 is automatic; Sentry and Net minimum 6, Remote Detonation 9. There is no source automatic Arch capstone. Mech Overdrive 20 is automatic: once/long rest when deploying choose one device whose duration becomes encounter end (maximum 1 minute), still command dependent, slot limited and destructible. No infinite pulses: healing effects keep original pulse cap and all per-use costs remain. Protected magic interface: once per short rest, as a Bonus Action route up to 2 current Dissonance into one of your active devices within 30 ft. Reduce Dissonance by that amount; the device is disabled and cannot move, attack, emit an aura or trigger effects until repaired or your next completed short rest. Its duration keeps ticking. Repair with an Action and 1 RP using Field Repair, or with 10 minutes and 1 RP using tinkers tools. No RP is created and no Refrain counter resets.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. At Warrior level 1 choose Strength or Dexterity as your Warrior ability; this choice is permanent in this draft. S = 1/2/3/4 at Warrior levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, chosen Warrior ability modifier). Warrior technique attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + chosen modifier. Warrior technique save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + chosen modifier. Source basis: approved Player Rulebook extract and preserved class registry.

The Warrior remains three distinct stages: Base Warrior at levels 1-2, Arch Juggernaut at levels 3-9, then one Hero path at levels 10-20: Wardborn, Ironskin or Dreadspawn. Mutation trees and serums supplement those stages rather than replacing them or functioning as parallel classes.

MUTATION SLOTS. At Warrior 1 you have one mutation slot; slot II unlocks at Warrior 5, slot III at Warrior 13 and slot IV at Warrior 20. During a completed short or long rest, equip one eligible mutation in each slot. Equipped mutations are dormant until activated unless their text explicitly says otherwise. You cannot equip the same named mutation twice.

ACTIVE MUTATIONS. Before Juggernaut Mutation Efficiency, only one equipped mutation can be active at a time. Mutation Efficiency raises the ordinary simultaneous-active limit to two. Transcendent, Apex Form and other explicit features can temporarily exceed that limit. Activating a mutation beyond the current limit ends one active mutation of your choice unless an explicit exception permits otherwise.

SERUM RESERVE. After a long rest prepare two serum doses, choosing one of the six serum profiles for each dose. At Warrior 11 the reserve becomes three prepared doses; at Warrior 20 it becomes four. Used doses do not naturally refill on a short rest. A long rest refills the reserve. Serum Recycling and explicit class features can preserve or restore doses, but no effect can increase the reserve above its current capacity.

SERUM INJECTION. Unless another feature says otherwise, injecting a prepared serum is a Bonus Action, consumes one prepared dose, activates one equipped mutation for 3 rounds and applies that dose's serum-profile benefits and side effect for the same 3 rounds. Reinjecting the same active mutation refreshes its duration rather than stacking it. Serum-profile numeric bonuses from two doses of the same profile never stack.

STRAIN. Begin after a long rest at 0 Strain; maximum Strain is 3. A normal serum injection or Mutagen Injection adds 1 Strain, Mutation Surge adds 1, and Serum Cocktail or Mutation Overload adds 2 unless modified. At Strain 2 your Speed is reduced by 5 feet. At Strain 3 you also take -1 AC and -1 on saving throws and cannot voluntarily activate another serum, Cocktail, Overclock or Surge until Strain is reduced. A completed short rest reduces Strain by 1; a long rest resets it to 0. Strain cannot exceed 3.

Mutation Adaptation and Serum Tolerance modify Strain and serum-profile side effects only as their cards state. A negative serum-profile side effect and Strain penalty are separate; preventing one does not automatically prevent the other.

BRUTALITY PROGRESS. Begin each real encounter with Brutality Progress 0 and BT 0. Add actual damage you personally deal to meaningful hostile creatures to Brutality Progress, but a single damage event contributes no more than one-quarter of your maximum HP. Crossing cumulative thresholds equal to 25%, 50% and 75% of your maximum HP grants 1 BT each, subject to the BT cap. Crossing 100% triggers Transcendent as described below but does not create a fourth stored BT unless Stack Overflow or another feature raises the cap.

TAKING DAMAGE AND BT. Once per round when one source deals you actual damage after mitigation equal to or greater than PB + M, gain 1 BT. This direct gain does not increase Brutality Progress. Normal threshold and damage-taken generation together can grant at most 2 BT per round. Explicit card gains such as Overpressure Response or Backlash Engine ignore that generation ceiling but never exceed the current BT cap.

BT CAP AND RESET. Default BT cap is 3. Stack Overflow raises it to 4. BT is not automatically spent; only features explicitly saying spend reduce it. Encounter end resets BT and Brutality Progress to 0. BT cannot be generated from friendly attacks, summoned sacrificial creatures, unattended objects, staged sparring or enemies that do not meaningfully threaten the party.

BRUTALITY STATES. At BT 1 you are Awakened; at BT 2 Primed; at BT 3 Unleashed. At Warrior 12+, reaching BT 4 or crossing 100% Brutality Progress may trigger the same once-per-encounter Transcendent pulse, even if your stored cap remains 3; it is never an indefinitely active state. State benefits are defined as operational extra Cards and vanish immediately if spending BT drops you below their thresholds.

HARD CONTROL GUARD. A creature can suffer at most one Warrior-caused effect that fully denies its normal turn, such as Stunned, Paralyzed or an equivalent full-turn denial, from your Warrior features per encounter. After the first succeeds, later Warrior effects from you that would fully deny that creature's turn instead remove its Reaction and reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of its next turn after the required save fails.

ADDITIONAL ACTION GUARD. All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot generate another Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Free attacks granted by Warrior features are explicitly bounded and never recursively grant additional free attacks.

RECHARGE GUARD. A named ability may receive at most one positive-counter reset or shortening per round. Only an ability with a positive recharge counter can be reset. Recharge never restores a spent short-rest or long-rest use unless the feature explicitly says it restores that use.

HEALING AND REGENERATION. Warrior healing cannot exceed maximum HP, restore the dead or remove Wounds unless a card explicitly says otherwise. Regeneration and repeated healing effects operate only during real encounters unless their card explicitly permits downtime healing. No corpse, summoned creature, trivial enemy or friendly target can be used to create infinite healing, serum doses or BT.

IMMUNITY AND RESISTANCE. Warrior resistance does not stack with resistance to the same damage type; apply one resistance. Immunity supersedes resistance but multiple immunities provide no additional benefit. If a feature grants several immunities temporarily, each is still only one immunity to that specific type or condition.

MUTATION TIERS. Basic mutations require Warrior 1. Advanced mutations require Warrior 6. Apex mutations require Warrior 15. You may equip any mutation whose level gate and other prerequisite you meet. Each tree permits any number of Basic mutations up to slot limits, at most two equipped Advanced mutations at once, and at most one equipped Apex mutation at once.

MUTATION FEATS. Mutation feats are not free mutation selections. They become eligible choices at an ASI/feat opportunity or other campaign feat grant once their listed level and mutation prerequisite are met. They do not consume mutation slots unless their own text says otherwise.

HERO MUTATION TREES. Bulwark Mutation Tree, Gore Mutation Tree and Aberrant Mutation Tree are Hero cards that unlock their associated Hero-specific mutation extra Cards. Those mutations still occupy normal mutation slots and obey active-mutation, serum and Strain rules.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Warrior 1 automatically gains Mutation Slot I and the BT tracker, then chooses 4 Base cards with at least 2 Active. Warrior 2 automatically gains Mutagen Injection, then chooses 2 additional Base cards. Warrior 3 enters Juggernaut and chooses 2 Arch cards with at least 1 Active. Warrior levels 4-9 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Source progression automatic features remain separate and never consume these choices.

At Warrior 10 choose Wardborn, Ironskin or Dreadspawn and choose 2 Hero cards from that path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Hero Final Form is automatic at Warrior 20 and cannot be selected early. ASI/feat grants remain separate.

SOURCE PROGRESSION RECONCILIATION. Book progression grants Mutation Slot II at 5, Bone Hardened at 6, Serum Overclock at 9, Mutation Slot III at 13, Brutal Adaptation at 15, Reflexive Mutation at 17 and Apex Form at 20 automatically. Registry-only Fighting Style, Second Wind, Action Surge, Extra Attack and draft level features are preserved in excluded Registry Alternatives and original source evidence. They are not acquired or stacked onto this playtest schedule.

All class gates use Warrior class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. No other class level unlocks Warrior mutation tiers, serum capacity, Juggernaut, Hero paths, Apex mutations or Final Forms.

Finite recovery completion: Mutation Recovery Reserve=3 L+M HP after a long rest. Bloodthick Node, Rapid Coagulation, Regenerative Mutation, Hemophage Core and their healing enhancements draw from this shared reserve, 1 point per actual HP healed. No short-rest refill; no gauge, critical hit, free activation or form change replenishes it. Other explicitly limited-use/dose healing retains its own printed limit. This new test reserve prevents indefinite regenerative healing from free mutation activations.
currentClassEngineComparisons.purpose: Actual class comparison; Bard uses its separate source schema. Feat assignments neither acquire nor rewrite these engines.

completeCurrentEngine: PROVISIONAL PLAYTEST CONTRACT. Intelligence is the Wizard class ability. S = 1/2/3/4 at Wizard levels 1/5/11/17. M = max(1, Intelligence modifier). Wizard spell attack = d20 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier. Wizard spell save DC = 8 + normal character proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

The Wizard remains three distinct stages: Base Wizard at levels 1-2, Arch Arcanist at levels 3-9, and one Hero path at levels 10-20: Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer. Hero paths are not additional starting classes and their features cannot be selected before their Wizard class-level gates.

SPELLBOOK. At Wizard 1 your spellbook contains six chosen rank-1 Wizard spells. Arcane School Specialization also adds one legal rank-1 bonus spell of your chosen school without replacing one of those six. For this provisional progression, add 2 legal Wizard spells to the book at each Wizard level 2-4, 3 at each level 5-8, 4 at each level 9-12, 5 at each level 13-16 and 6 at each level 17-20. Level-up additions cost no money or scribing time.

LEGAL RANKS. Maximum Wizard spell rank by Wizard class level is: rank 1 at levels 1-2, rank 2 at 3-4, rank 3 at 5-6, rank 4 at 7-8, rank 5 at 9-10, rank 6 at 11-12, rank 7 at 13-14, rank 8 at 15-16 and rank 9 at 17-20. Grand Tier at level 20 is a special casting permission, not a tenth ordinary rank. A Wizard may learn Wizard-list spells from any school up to the legal rank unless a spell itself has an additional prerequisite.

PREPARED SPELL MATRIX. After a long rest, prepare a number of matrices equal to Wizard level + Intelligence modifier, minimum 1, selecting only spells currently recorded in your spellbook and within your legal rank. You cast ordinary Wizard spells only from prepared matrices unless a feature explicitly overrides that restriction. Preparing the full daily matrix set normally requires 1 hour of spellbook study. Matrix Efficiency reduces this to 45 minutes.

DUPLICATE PREPARATION. You may prepare the same spell more than once, primarily to carry different Matrix Mastery configurations. Duplicate copies never create additional first-cast Dissonance exemptions. For Refrain and the protected strain rule, all prepared copies sharing the same underlying spell name belong to one matrix family regardless of modification.

MIDDAY SUBSTITUTION. Once between long rests, you may perform a 10-minute Spellbook Study ritual to replace one prepared matrix with another legal spell from your spellbook. The replacement cannot exceed your legal Wizard rank. Sigil Rewrite and Matrix Mastery may improve this process as explicitly stated.

SPELL ACQUISITION BY SCRIBING. A found Wizard spell may be copied into the spellbook if its rank is legal for you. Baseline scribing requires 2 hours and 50 gp of inks/materials per spell rank, treating rank 0 as 1 for this calculation. Spell Scribing halves both values to 1 hour and 25 gp per rank. Failure to finish the work consumes no spellbook entry but materials already expended during an interrupted hour are lost.

SPELLBOOK LOSS. Losing the spellbook does not erase matrices currently prepared in memory; you may continue casting those prepared matrices until you next rebuild or change preparation. A blank replacement book can be seeded with your currently prepared spells at 1 hour and 25 gp per effective spell rank each. An unprepared spell you previously recorded can be reconstructed from memory with 8 hours, 100 gp per rank and an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 + spell rank. Failure consumes that attempt's time and half its materials; another attempt can be made after a long rest. Recovering the original book automatically restores access to its surviving entries.

ARCANE SCHOOL SPECIALIZATION is automatic at Wizard 1. Choose exactly one of the eight schools. Your spell attacks with that school gain +1 and your Wizard save DC for that school's spells gains +1. You also add one legal rank-1 spell of that school to the spellbook. The source table explicitly supplies seven school passives; the eighth core school, Abjuration, is named elsewhere but its passive row is missing. Its provisional playtest passive is identified below rather than silently presented as recovered text.

ABJURATION, provisional completion for the omitted eighth row: once per round after you cast an Abjuration spell, gain temporary HP equal to PB until the start of your next regular turn. CONJURATION: creatures summoned by your Wizard spells gain +1 maximum HP per Wizard level. DIVINATION: once per long rest reroll one failed saving throw and use the new result. ENCHANTMENT: when a creature fails its initial save against one of your Enchantment spells, a printed control duration of at least 1 round may last one additional round, but every normally allowed repeat save still occurs. EVOCATION: when casting an area Evocation spell, exclude one creature from its initial damaging area; that creature automatically succeeds and takes no damage if success normally halves damage. ILLUSION: gain +2 on concentration saves made to maintain Illusion spells. NECROMANCY: once per turn during a real encounter when a hostile non-summoned creature dies from your Necromancy spell, gain 1 temporary HP; it is not permanent healing. TRANSMUTATION: after casting a Transmutation spell, gain +5 feet Speed until the end of that turn.

PROTECTED DISSONANCE INTERFACE. The first cast of each different prepared matrix family during an encounter generates 0 BASE Dissonance. This exemption affects only base strain. Refrain and explicitly printed strain costs still apply; the suite disables generic Overcast and does not layer historical Burn onto Dissonance. Repeating a matrix family follows normal Refrain immediately. Preparing duplicates or differently modified copies of the same underlying spell never refreshes the exemption.

Core Systems V 2 Resonance Points and spell-rank RP costs are authoritative for Wizard spellcasting. There are no historical spell slots in this pilot. Wizard cards tagged wizard-spell are always-prepared class matrices once acquired, do not consume a daily prepared-matrix position and use the same RP, concentration, Refrain and protected first-distinct-matrix rules as other Wizard spells. Their printed RP cost replaces any generic rank cost; never pay both.

RITUAL CASTING is automatic at Wizard 2. A Wizard spell in your spellbook with the Ritual tag can be cast from the book without being prepared by increasing its casting time by at least 10 minutes. A ritual cast costs 0 RP unless that ritual explicitly lists a consumed RP cost, cannot be used during an encounter and cannot generate or vent Dissonance through ordinary casting strain.

Only one concentration effect can normally be maintained. Starting a second concentration effect ends the first. Damage uses the current Core Systems concentration rule; required half-damage rounding is down for this pilot. Spell Tether and the level-17 Tethered Cast are the only Wizard-specific exceptions in this draft, and each has an explicit RP price, duration and one-tether cap.

MATRIX MASTERY MODIFICATIONS. After acquiring Matrix Mastery, each prepared ordinary spell matrix may carry at most one modification chosen during preparation. QUICK SUBSTITUTION: once per short rest, replace one matrix marked Quick Substitution with another spellbook spell of exactly the same rank using a 1-minute ritual instead of the normal 10-minute midday swap; the replacement loses the modification until the next long rest. COMPONENT ENHANCEMENT: when casting a damaging or healing matrix, spend 1 additional RP to add one extra die of the spell's primary damage or healing die to one roll; if the spell has no such die this modification has no effect. MATRIX LINKING: pair two different prepared matrix families during preparation; after legally casting one, the other costs 1 less RP, minimum 1, if cast before the end of your next regular turn, at most once per pair per round. STABILITY REINFORCEMENT: gain +2 on concentration saves caused by damage while maintaining that matrix. A matrix modification never creates another spell cast or proc event.

All sources share a maximum of one additional full Action per creature per round. Additional Actions cannot grant another additional Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Spell copies, Matrix Sharing, Arcane Fusion, Dual Cast and similar effects pay all explicitly required RP and do not produce duplicate resource, cast-proc or action-grant chains beyond their written resolution.

Round recharge counters decrease once at the start of your regular initiative turn even if you cannot act. Extra Actions and extra turns do not tick recharge. Outside initiative, each uninterrupted 6 seconds counts as one tick. Only positive counters can be reset or shortened and each named ability can receive at most one reset or shortening per round.

SUMMON COMMAND LIMIT. All Wizard-controlled conjured, raised and bound companions share one damaging/control Companion Command per Wizard regular turn. Spend one Bonus Action to command exactly one such creature to move up to its Speed and use one damaging or control action from its stat block. Uncommanded creatures may reposition defensively and take Dodge but cannot deal damage or impose conditions. No summoned or raised creature can create XP, treasure, RP, Dissonance relief, additional corpses or kill-resource farms.

NECROMANCER STANDARD UNDEAD. Corpse Harvest and Auto-Raise share a maximum of three standard raised minions. Skeleton: AC 14, HP 6 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Bone Shot, range 30 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. Zombie: AC 12, HP 10 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 20; Slam, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. Goblin Thrall, available only from a goblinoid corpse: AC 13, HP 8 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30; Shiv, reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d6+S necrotic. These are pre-Flesh-Ascendant statistics.

NECROMANCER AUTO-RAISE. Once per round when one of your standard undead minions personally lands the killing blow on an eligible humanoid and your standard-minion count is below three, its corpse rises at the end of the current turn as the same mechanical minion type that scored the kill, if physically possible. A new minion cannot act during that same round. Auto-Raise costs no Action or RP but can never exceed the three-minion cap or generate a new resource, corpse chain, XP or treasure event. Without Infernal Pact only humanoids qualify.

ELITE UNDEAD PETS. Necromancers may bind Boneflayer, Dreadblade and Wraithbound, at most one of each and three elite pets total. They use the same shared Companion Command limit as standard undead. Boneflayer: AC 14, HP 12 + 2 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Bone Shards: range 60, Wizard spell attack, 2d6+S necrotic. Fear Pulse replaces its attack: enemies within 10 feet make Wisdom saves; failure Frightened until end of next turn; recharge 3. Grave Miasma replaces its attack: 10-foot-radius point within 30 feet until start of your next turn; enemies entering or starting there take 1d6 necrotic once; recharge 3.

Dreadblade: AC 16, HP 16 + 3 × Wizard level, Speed 30. Disrupting Blade: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic; a concentrating target immediately makes its concentration save with disadvantage. On a natural 20 the target is Weakened until the end of its next turn, taking -1 on attack rolls. Dreadblade has advantage on saves against forced movement.

Wraithbound: AC 14, HP 10 + 2 × Wizard level, Fly 40 and hover. While it has not attacked or imposed control since the end of its previous turn it is Invisible; attacking ends that state until the end of its next turn. Wraith Strike: reach 5 feet, Wizard spell attack, 1d8+S necrotic. On natural 20 the target makes a Constitution save against your Wizard DC; failure Stuns until the end of its next turn.

Flesh Ascendant's bonus applies after the listed base statistics: every undead creature you control gains +2 maximum HP per Wizard level. If at least two of your undead creatures are active, each gains +1 AC and +1 on saving throws. This does not increase the standard-minion or elite-pet caps.

DARK-TRAUMA INTERFACE. Necromancer features involving corpse desecration, infernal bargains, domination, body control or Mind Prison remain subject to the project's existing dark-content and trauma boundaries. A table may fade description to black without changing mechanics. No feature changes a player's real belief, permanently transfers ownership of a player character or silently retires a PC.

PROPOSED ACQUISITION. Wizard 1 automatically gains Arcane School Specialization, Spell Matrix System and the starting spellbook, then chooses 4 selectable Base cards, at least 2 Active. Wizard 2 automatically gains Counterspell and Ritual Casting, then chooses 2 additional selectable Base cards. Counterspell is not also placed in the Arch selection pool.

At Wizard 3 enter Arcanist, automatically gain Arcane Tradition as an upgrade of the SAME level-1 school rather than choosing another school, and choose 2 selectable Arch cards, at least 1 Active. Wizard 4 grants one eligible Base/Arch choice. Wizard 5 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic School Mastery. Wizard 6 grants one Base/Arch choice plus automatic Arcane Ward. Wizard 7 grants one eligible Arch choice. Wizard 8 grants one Base/Arch choice. Wizard 9 grants one eligible Arch choice plus automatic Dual Cast.

At Wizard 10 choose Spellbinder, Elementalist or Necromancer and gain 2 Hero cards from that path. ELEMENTALIST EXCEPTION: Elemental Affinity is automatic at path selection and counts as one of those two level-10 Hero acquisitions, so an Elementalist chooses only one additional Hero card at level 10. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base/Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. The chosen Final Theorem is automatic at Wizard 20. School Mastery, Counterspell, Arcane Tradition and all progression-table automatic features are never duplicated as selections.

All acquisition gates use Wizard class level rather than total character level. Normal proficiency bonus follows the game's ordinary total-character-level rule. A multiclass dip cannot unlock higher spell ranks, Arcanist cards, Hero cards, Final Theorems or progression-table features.

Class matrices tagged wizard-spell receive a rank in normalized card data equal to maximum ordinary Wizard rank at their minimum class-level gate (cap 9). Printed RP cost replaces generic rank cost. Counterspell is rank 1 at its explicit level 2 automatic grant. This explicit convention closes rank-dependent Counterspell/Dissonance interactions without inventing extra costs.

Cantrip completion: know 3 Wizard cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10, using the shared missing-repertoire fallback. Cantrips are known directly and do not consume prepared matrices. Always-prepared class matrices are additional cards, not extra arbitrary ordinary spells. Class spell ranks and the normalized activation field resolve incomplete source terminology.

actualCard.name: Beast Companion
actualCard.cost: 4 RP; 1 hour with a willing/tamed eligible beast
actualCard.effect: Bond eligible beast using standard companion stats plus Wisdom modifier HP; preserve one movement mode up to 40 ft and keen-sense advantage. Bonus Action command gives one attack, no imported boss powers. Injury persists; heal normally. Death requires a new bond after long rest, not free resummoning.

source.originalText: Beast Companion: Tame one beast from the bestiary (CR ≤ your level, INT < 7, not corrupted) as a permanent companion that scales with your Wisdom and level.

completeCurrentEngine: Dexterity governs weapons; Wisdom governs primal technique DC/M. This draft uses the detailed book's d8 Hit Die; older runtime d10 remains preserved as a conflicting alternative. At 1 gain Track Target engine: Bonus Action mark one perceived enemy within 90 ft for 1 minute, no RP, one quarry at a time; new mark replaces old. Once/own turn a weapon hit against quarry adds S damage. Mark does not reveal creatures through total cover. Track Target selection is an upgrade, not a second unlock tax.

Weapon Synergy tracks last successful direct weapon hit on your own turns. Changing melee→ranged grants+1 to that ranged attack roll if it is your first attack of the turn; changing ranged→melee makes the hit apply Bleed 1d4 on target's next 2 turns. Once/turn synergy; Do Ts, copies, companions, forced attacks and misses do not advance it. At 5 ordinary Attack Action makes two attacks; techniques use only printed counts. You may draw/stow one weapon as normal object interaction; Dual Style later improves this.

Elemental Attunement is defensive; Elemental Imbue is the separate Pathfinder feature gated 6. Imbue Bonus Action 2 RP, one element for 3 of your turns; once/turn a weapon hit adds 1d4 of chosen element plus fire:Burn 1d4 next target turn, cold:Speed-10 ft until end next turn, poison:CON save or-1 attack rolls until end next turn. Nonstacking; Do Ts never build Hit Chain. Switching element pays again.

Druidic Arrow Combo starts at Ranger 11, not at Base 1. Each direct successful weapon hit adds 1 Hit Chain, maximum 2 gained per regular turn and cap 3. Completing 3 primes one Arrow until end next turn; using it consumes the chain, even on miss. Efficient Killer lowers threshold 2. Chain starts/ends encounters 0, cannot be stocked against allies/captives/summons and is cleared by incapacitation. The Arrow is one Action with a ranged weapon attack or the stated save, costs 0 RP when primed, and is a magical class technique rather than an ordinary spell cast. At most one Arrow per round; it cannot advance its own chain. It requires a wielded bow and ammunition. Ordinary attack/damage riders apply once as printed, never another free arrow.

All Rangers learn five bounded Arrows at 11. Emberroot requires the previous 3 successful weapon hits carried fire imbue: ranged attack, weapon+S d6 fire on hit; up to 2 others within 5 ft take S fire, and primary target Burns 1d4 next turn. Glacial Thorn requires 2 ranged+1 melee among those 3 hits: ranged attack weapon+S d6 cold; on hit STR save or Speed 0 until end next turn. Venomlash requires poisoned/blighted terrain at you or target: ranged attack weapon+S d6 poison; on hit CON save or-1 damage on its next attack. Spirit Fang requires quarry: ranged attack at advantage, weapon+S d6 force; ignores resistance but not immunity on the added force only. Cleansing Grove requires natural terrain at you or target: up to 3 living allies within 10 ft of a point within 60 ft each end Frightened or Poisoned; no attack or damage.

Chosen Hero grants a sixth Arrow at 11. Warder Nature's Wrath: ranged attack weapon+S d6 piercing; up to 2 allies within 10 ft gain M temporary HP (finite mitigation, not repeatable real healing). Stalker Phantom: two ranged attacks against different aligned targets within 60 ft, each weapon damage, no extra dice; one Arrow activation. Outrider Corruption: place 10 ft-radius zone within 60 ft, concentration until start next turn; up to 3 enemies entering/starting there take S d4 necrotic once each, CON half. Arrow copies cannot generate extra attacks, resources or permanent terrain changes.

A successful direct weapon hit between ordinary spell casts clears Refrain and gives the next ordinary spell before end next turn 1 less Dissonance, minimum 0. The benefit is single-use/nonstacking; it reduces neither RP nor both base and repeat separately. Ordinary spells use Ranger rank gates and the shared test magic configuration.

Base choices 1–2, Pathfinder Arch 3–9, and chosen Warder/Stalker/Outrider Hero 10–20 are distinct stages. No source Arch capstone/Finale exists: level 9 receives its normal eligible choice, while 20 automatically improves your Hero Arrow once/long rest (new capstone below). Do not acquire a Hero by spending Base choices. Beast Companion is one permanent bond; it must be a willing/tamed noncorrupted beast with INT<7 and CR no greater than your class level. Its combat profile uses the bounded companion below rather than importing a full CR 20 monster.

If a primed Arrow expires unused, the prime ends and Hit Chain resets to 0. This applies equally to Efficient Killer’s threshold of two. Efficient Killer itself requires Ranger 11, when Hit Chain exists.

actualCard.name: Coordinated Maneuver
actualCard.rangeAndTarget: One willing ally within 30 ft who hears you
actualCard.effect: Ally spends Reaction to move up to half Speed and make one weapon attack. This is one granted attack, not a full Attack Action; no Extra Attack. For cap purposes this granted move plus one weapon attack counts as the ally’s one additional full Action for the round; it still permits only one weapon attack and never Extra Attack.

source.originalText: Coordinated Maneuver: Direct an ally to move and take an action out of turn.

completeCurrentEngine: A martial class with d10 Hit Die, all armor and shields, repeating crossbows, sidearms and siege tools. Dexterity governs ranged attacks; Constitution governs class DC/M and defensive techniques. No RP, ordinary spellcasting, Refrain or Dissonance engine. Names such as Divine Lockdown describe disciplined suppression; they do not grant divine magic.

Overwatch is an automatic Base engine at 1. Bonus Action designate a visible 15 ft square within weapon range until start next regular turn. Once during that interval, spend your Reaction when a perceived enemy enters, moves inside, attacks an ally from, or reveals itself inside the zone. Make one legal ranged attack with ammunition and line of fire, normally 1d8+DEX piercing. On hit choose Snare (Speed-10 ft until end next turn), Bleed (1d4 at start next turn), or Push 5 ft (STR save negates push). Concealment still applies. Only one Overwatch zone; no extra Reaction. The optional Overwatch card upgrades this engine. At 17 you may move 5 ft without opportunity attacks after its shot, once/round.

At 5 automatically gain Palisade Deployment. Spend one carried barricade kit and an Action to erect a 2-by 1-tile wall in contiguous unoccupied ground within 5 ft. Height 5 ft, AC 12, HP 5+CON modifier minimum 1, immunity psychic/poison; blocks movement and line of sight across its full height but can be climbed using 10 ft movement. One kit/use per encounter, two at 13; a long rest with carpentry tools replenishes 2 kits (carried maximum 2, reusable parts have no resale value). Material is required; no conjuring. At most one intact wall, two at 13. Old wall must be dismantled in 1 minute before replacement beyond cap. Once per encounter an Action repairs a wall for M HP using spare parts; destruction does not refresh uses.

Palisade Tier II at 13 doubles wall HP and grants resistance to damage from area effects. Hold Position: while adjacent to your intact wall gain+1 AC and+1 saves. Brace Line: an ally immediately behind you relative to a ranged attacker, with your wall adjacent to both of you, has 2 flat DR against that attacker. These bonuses do not stack with another Soldier wall; strongest flat DR applies. Full cover prevents attacks rather than granting an additional AC bonus.

Base 1–2, Commander Arch 3–9, then Champion/Artillerist/Tyrant Hero 10–20. Palisade 5 is automatic; Intercepting Shot has minimum 6 and Fortify Zone 9. Other cards require selection. There is no source automatic Arch capstone. At 20 gain the new Final Command below, clearly a playtest addition. No spell or sustained technique may be used to obtain infinite ammunition, structures, actions or permanent healing.

sourceObject.name: War Caster
sourceObject.description: You have practiced casting spells in the midst of combat.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Which rule applies
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Which rule applies

The domain authority is [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx). The approved [Player Rulebook V6](../../../../books/player/Decennium_Descent_Player_Rulebook_v6.docx) supplies compatible rules that Core does not replace. This overlay states the selected interpretation or newly authored rule wherever those sources leave a gap. An explicit exception on an operative, reviewed class/spell/item card applies only within its printed scope; a historical alternate or a same-named feature is not an extra grant. This candidate does not promote an entire historical branch.

| Question | Active rule and provenance | Inactive alternate |
|---|---|---|
| Attacks | Core V2: meet AC; natural 1 misses; natural 20 hits and doubles damage dice. | Applying the general Gameplay four-degree roll to attacks. |
| Task checks | Explicitly adopted Gameplay four degrees and natural shifts. | Assuming every critical result creates an unprinted effect. |
| Ordinary saves | Binary meet-DC test; printed failure margins remain literal. Natural 1/20 do not generically shift saves in this candidate. This separation is an integration choice. | Automatic critical saves or natural-result shifts inferred from the task rule. |
| Death-save timing | Core and V6: start of turn; regular-turn-only timing is a provisional guard. | Gameplay end-of-turn saves. |
| Wounds | Core trigger/save, Constitution-save and Hit-Dice-recovery penalties, and three-Wound Critical state. | Gameplay automatic Wound triggers, Hit Dice healing penalty, half Speed and Strain lock. |
| Named Wounded condition | Core paragraph 782 expressly describes the same Wound count, Constitution penalty, Hit Dice recovery and three-Wound Critical state. Apply those records once. | V6 Appendix A paragraphs 9971–9974 give a conflicting temporary condition cleared by magic/rest with Constitution-save disadvantage; Core replaces it here. |
| Stable, instant death, knockout and temporary HP | Compatible recovered V6 rules. | Treating these recovered rules as newly invented. |
| Ordinary Wound treatment | Explicit Gameplay-derived integration below. | Claiming it is original Core wording or ordinary HP healing. |
| Injury table and unresolved thresholds | New provisional choices below, with their search limits stated. | Dropping Core's failure-by-5 consequence because its table was not located. |

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Rolls
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Rolls

Choose the roll type before rolling. Use the actual ability modifier, including negative values, and normal proficiency only when applicable. Existing advantage/disadvantage chooses the higher/lower of two d20s; multiple sources do not stack, and any advantage plus disadvantage cancels. Add other legal modifiers once. Fractions round down unless a rule specifies otherwise. One tile is 5 feet. Class L, S and effect M retain their definitions in the shared class rules.

**Attack:** roll d20 plus the appropriate attack modifier against AC. Meeting AC hits. Natural 1 always misses; natural 20 always hits and critically doubles damage dice, not flat modifiers. Beating AC by 10 is not a critical hit. An explicit broader critical range does not stack with another; use the broadest eligible range. In this overlay, a natural result below 20 in that range must still meet AC unless the feature expressly says it always hits.

**Task, skill or tool check against a fixed DC:** total at least DC+10 is Critical Success; at least DC is Success; at most DC-10 is Critical Failure; other totals below DC are Failure. Natural 20 then improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one, bounded at either end. A task printing only success/failure collapses the two upper degrees to success and two lower degrees to failure; no extra consequence is invented. A natural 20 can still fail an otherwise impossible check, and a natural 1 with sufficient modifiers can still succeed.

**Saving throw:** total at least DC succeeds; otherwise it fails. Natural 1 and 20 have no generic special outcome. A printed failure by 5 or 10 compares the final total with the DC; it does not add an unprinted critical-save system. Death saves are the specific exception below.

**Opposed check, new provisional tie rule:** compare final totals. Higher wins; an exact tie leaves the existing state unchanged, so the initiating creature fails to change it. Do not turn task natural shifts into hidden numeric modifiers. A maneuver explicitly printing degree outcomes must specify how those apply.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Resolve a damage event
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Resolve a damage event

Resolve each genuinely separate hit or damage event once. Do not split one packet to multiply Wound saves or combine separate hits merely to cross a threshold. Feature-specific prevention that acts before damage or before reaching zero resolves at its printed timing first.

1. Resolve attack/save, damage and applicable defenses. The remaining nonnegative amount is **resolved damage**.
2. Record HP, Wounds and zero-HP state before the event. Remove temporary HP first. **Post-temp damage = resolved damage minus temporary HP absorbed.** Keep this amount even when it exceeds current HP; floor the resulting current HP at zero.
3. Check V6 Instant Death. If post-temp damage minus HP before the hit is at least maximum HP, the creature dies. For a creature already at zero, this is post-temp damage at least maximum HP. Stop: there is no Wound save, death-save failure or successful knockout from that event.
4. Otherwise, a living creature makes one Wound save if it dropped from positive HP to zero, if **2 × post-temp damage is at least maximum HP**, or if the effect actually inflicts Maiming. Overlapping triggers still cause only one save. The post-temp threshold and one-save rule are new provisional interpretations. Maiming is an independent trigger even when temporary HP absorbs all ordinary damage; immunity to Maiming itself still applies.
5. Make a Constitution save against **max(10, floor(post-temp damage / 2))**. Use pre-event Wounds for the -1-per-Wound penalty. Maiming with zero post-temp damage uses DC 10. A Wound gained now cannot penalize the roll that created it.
6. A success adds no Wound. A failure that began with zero, one or two Wounds adds exactly one; failure by 5 or more also gives that Wound one Injury. A failure that began with three Wounds kills the creature instead: no fourth Wound and no Injury roll. Stop processing later living-target consequences if dead.
7. If the creature was already at zero before this event and post-temp damage is positive, end Stable. A creature using death saves adds one failure, or two for a critical hit; three failures kill it. An ordinary creature that does not use death saves dies instead, without starting death counters. A hit from positive HP to zero does not also cause a same-packet death failure.
8. If this event newly reduces positive HP to zero, a valid melee knockout makes the surviving creature Stable. Otherwise a character/significant NPC using death saves begins dying; an ordinary monster dies. A previously Stable creature whose temporary HP absorbed all damage remains Stable unless an independent Maiming result killed it. The Director identifies significant NPCs consistently. Knockout cannot override Instant Death or a fatal Wound save.

Core's Maiming and Wound trigger rules remain subject to an actual feature's eligibility. The reference helper receives already legal events; it does not grant every attack Maiming or a damage-prevention exception.

currentGoverningExcerpts.heading: Zero HP and recovery
currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
## Zero HP and recovery

A living character at zero HP is Unconscious. Core's condition already includes Incapacitated, unawareness, dropping held items and falling Prone; an adjacent hit is critical as specified there. Healing does not silently remove other independent causes of Unconscious or Prone.

While dying, make one death save at the **start of each regular initiative turn**. Roll d20 without modifiers unless a feature specifically modifies death saves. Natural 20 restores 1 HP; natural 1 adds two failures. Other results of 10 or more add one success; 9 or less add one failure. Three successes make the creature Stable; three failures make it Dead. Extra turns and Actions add no extra death saves. Stable or Dead creatures do not roll them.

Regaining positive HP or becoming Stable resets both counters. Temporary HP does not raise normal HP, end Unconscious or reset counters. Fully absorbed damage does not end Stable or add a death failure in this provisional interpretation. Independent Maiming can still cause its Wound save.

**Stabilize:** an Action and DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or an Action using one healer's-kit use automatically, stabilizes a living dying creature at zero. It remains Unconscious and makes no death saves. Roll 1d4 once when it becomes Stable and record its absolute recovery time that many hours later. If still Stable then, it regains 1 HP. Damage reaching normal HP cancels that deadline and resumes dying with the appropriate failures. Rest and Stable recovery use the same elapsed clock, so four hours of recovery inside an eight-hour Watch do not cost twelve hours. A later rest does not separately replay the Stable healing event.

**Dead:** ordinary healing and stabilization do not restore life. Resurrection must satisfy its own willing-soul, body, time, cost and target rules. It does not automatically remove Wounds, Corruption, debts, legal death or claims upon the body. Corpses cannot supply repeated resource triggers.

# Combat, actions and timing — provisional playtest integration

**Status: REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the supplied combat/action/timing/vision scope.** [GPT's disposition](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_STRAIN_FIRST_REVIEW.md) confirms the corrected candidate. This does not close all combat, movement, encounter or condition work. Original books, class cards and earlier drafts are preserved. The NEW decisions below apply to this candidate only.

Read alongside [core resolution and injury](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md), [conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md), [custom riders](CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md), [spell integration](SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md) and [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md). This document explicitly supersedes conflicting provisional clauses only where listed. A specific reviewed feature retains its printed costs, prerequisites and exceptions.

## Source decisions

The [exact packet](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/COMBAT_ACTION_VISION_SOURCE_PACKET.json) contains 217 paragraphs from unchanged Core V2 and V6 books. Paragraph indices are zero-based all Word XML `w:p` descendants. [Source validation](COMBAT_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) verifies quotations and whole-book hashes. The [first GPT proposal](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_ACTION_TIMING_FIRST_REVIEW.md), [counterexamples](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/CODEX_COMBAT_COUNTEREXAMPLES.md) and [revised decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_COUNTEREXAMPLE_REVIEW.md) preserve the conference.

| Topic | Source / conflict | Candidate decision |
|---|---|---|
| Initiative, action list, encounter clock | Core 373–418 | Core controls; compatible V6 8066–8244 supplies detailed procedures. |
| Reaction | Core/V6 summarize one per round; V6 and class integration refresh own turn | NEW explicit interpretation: one resource between regular own-turn starts; no global-round reset. |
| Stances | Core 419–435; extra-turn ambiguity | Keep listed effects; NEW regular-turn selection and finite allowances. |
| Movement | Core 436–458; V6 mode switching subtracts physical distance | NEW spent-cost ledger prevents terrain/standing refunds; multiple legal Dashes each add Speed. |
| Maneuvers | Core 460–486 | Preserve sourced effects; NEW declaration, costs and endpoints fill missing execution details. |
| Grapple/Shove | V6 opposed procedure vs older shared-class generic DC | Ordinary maneuvers use V6 opposed rolls. Printed card saves/DCs retain their scope. |
| Prone and Invisible | Core/V6 conflicts already reviewed | Current condition reference controls, including Core ranged Prone disadvantage and Invisible position-reveal exception. |
| Round duration / simultaneous events | Sources do not give complete ordering | NEW preserved virtual markers and explicit start/end sequence below. |
| Ready | V6 casts and holds spell; generic Action or movement | Preserve that procedure; NEW one pending state and preparation/release details. |
| Hide/Search | Core lists actions; V6 unseen attacks | NEW passive DC and observer-specific Hidden procedure using Core task degrees. |
| Diagonals / terrain composition | 5-ft tile convention; missing full composition | NEW equal orthogonal/diagonal metric and additive movement costs. |
| Periodic and falling clocks | Existing reviewed overlays | Remain authoritative in their stated scope; no extra-turn tick or duplicated fall step. |
| Equipment, cargo and Sunder | Core delegates actual object/cargo systems | No invented durability, capacity or automatic cargo protection. These dependencies remain open. |

## Encounter and action resources

Establish terrain, light, hazards, objectives, exits and cargo; determine awareness; roll `d20 + DEX modifier + legal bonuses`. Highest first. Players choose player/player ties; the Director resolves ties involving NPCs. Keep the resulting ordered slots for the encounter. A round represents approximately six seconds. A **regular turn** is a creature's normal initiative slot even if it cannot act. An extra turn is distinct.

A turn normally permits movement, one Action, a Bonus Action when an actual rule grants a use, and one ordinary free object interaction. A second ordinary interaction or an Action-time object activation uses an Action. Brief communication is not an extra Action. Conditions and specific features may restrict these permissions.

The shared limit is one **extra full Action per creature per numbered round**. Such an Action cannot grant another extra Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. This cap is independent of Reaction timing. Extra turns do not by themselves refresh Reactions, recharge, periodic ticks, recovery ticks or the regular-turn allowances defined here.

**Reaction interpretation.** Begin an encounter with one available Reaction unless surprised or otherwise prohibited. Refresh at each regular own-turn start; never at the numbered round boundary or an extra turn. A late-initiative creature can therefore react before its first turn, refresh, and react again in the same numbered round. A legal trigger, available resource and all feature prerequisites are still required.

**Explicit additional Reactions.** A reviewed card can grant a separate limited use without refreshing the ordinary resource. Warrior Mind Shock supplies its stated once-per-duration non-attack Reaction; spending one resource does not consume/reset the other. Surprise, Incapacitated and Focused still restrict both. It grants no Counterspell knowledge or waived costs. Extra turns refresh neither. Per-dose reapplication/stacking and other specific grants remain part of the class semantic pass.

**Surprise — V6 plus NEW Bonus Action clarification.** On a surprised creature's first regular turn it cannot voluntarily move or take an Action or Bonus Action. It cannot react until that turn ends. Its slot, durations, passive effects, concentration, periodic effects and recharge still occur. Surprise alone is not Incapacitated or Unconscious. Brief communication and an otherwise legal simple free interaction remain possible.

**Entry — NEW.** Standard end-round reinforcements roll/receive initiative and first act next round. An explicit midround entrant acts this round only if its complete ordered slot is still upcoming; entry during that exact slot counts as already passed. It has its initial Reaction unless prohibited. A summon-specific timing rule overrides this generic entry procedure.

After the final slot, resolve Core's end-round hazards, reinforcements, morale, objectives and boss phases. Conclude the scene with surrender, capture, pursuit, harvesting access and noise consequences under their own rules; winning initiative does not resolve those automatically.

## Time and event ordering — NEW

For a duration created in initiative, record the relevant original regular start/end marker. Existing effects keep that **virtual marker**, repeating every six seconds if the creature leaves or changes initiative. Reordering, rerolling, extra turns, death/removal or leaving/reentering initiative never restart an existing duration. New effects use the current schedule. Source death still ends concentration, a source-dependent aura/tether or an effect explicitly ending on death.

- A bare hostile target-bound **N rounds** ends at the Nth future regular target-end marker. An in-progress target turn's current end does not count.
- A bare self/source buff, ally-targeted buff or source-controlled aura **N rounds** ends at the Nth future source-start marker. Explicit target-turn, pulse or absolute timing overrides this default. Activation during source turn 1 for three rounds ends at source turn 4's start.
- **Next turn** means the next future regular turn of the named creature, not the current turn's still-upcoming end. An unqualified next turn refers to source/user under the existing shared rule. Explicit “this turn” can include the current turn.
- An outside-initiative bare N-round effect instead gets an absolute application-time + N×6 seconds deadline. Entering initiative preserves that deadline.
- Explicit periodic profiles retain their registered clocks and tick counts. Never create a second timer merely because a generic duration rule also exists.

The [exact GPT review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_COMBAT_EXACT_FINDINGS.md) confirms ally-buff source clocks and excluding the current turn for explicit next-turn endpoints.
